routes.how_it_works: A Chift client becomes a Horus company (the third-party record of a folder) flagged as customer and created with companies.new. Creation returns only an id, so the connector then reads the company, its IBANs and its receivable account back to build the Chift response.
routes.documented: companies.new creates the company in a folder and requires FolderId, SearchKey, Name, IsCustomer, IsSupplier, IsVatLiable, LanguageCode and CountryCode (guide: Managing customers & suppliers). One call carries name, VAT number, one address, phone, website, emails, external reference, IBANs and the receivable (concentration) account. Create calls return only the new id (guide: Responses & errors); companies.info and ibans.list return the stored data. One company can be customer and supplier at once, and companies.update is a partial update, so force_merge maps to setting IsCustomer on the existing supplier. A VAT number already used by another company is refused by default, and search keys are unique within the folder.
depends_on_assumption: The search key (third-party code) is generated from the client name, numeric suffix on collision (Proposal, C8); Horus length and character rules are undocumented.
Required Horus fields Chift may not send are filled by rule: VAT liability from vat; language and country from folder defaults when missing (Proposal).
active=false is written as CustomerActivitySuspended=true, a field whose meaning is undocumented.
company_number of a non-VAT-liable client is stored as VatNumber with IsVatLiable=false; no documented write field exists for the enterprise number.
Phone and website written as PhoneNumber and Website come back as ContactPhone and ContactWebsite (pairing deduced from field names).
Duplicate protection rests on a pre-check by VAT number and external reference (Proposal); Horus documents no idempotency key.
needs_confirmation: Horus: search-key rules (maximum length, characters, case) and the error returned for a duplicate key (H7, H6).
Horus: meaning of CustomerActivitySuspended, Address2 and ContactPerson; how an enterprise number is written; default receivable account (H11).
Horus: is the duplicate-VAT check per folder, and does it ignore spaces and dots in VAT numbers (H25)?
Chift: search-key convention for new clients, and behaviour on a duplicate or a same-name client without VAT number (C8, C6).
Chift: force_merge policy (fill empty supplier fields or overwrite; conflicting external reference) (C6).
Chift: which address is kept when several are sent, and whether unstorable fields are rejected or dropped (C3).
not_concluded: Whether a create that timed out can still be committed later; until known, the check before a retry is best effort only (H3).
Whether sideloading on companies.list can return IBANs and the receivable account, cutting the read-back to one call (include paths undocumented, H15).
routes.feasibility_reason: Creation, read-back and merge are documented; only the search-key format, a few field meanings and the duplicate policy rest on assumptions or Chift decisions, and none blocks the build.

considerations.text: A Horus 'company' is a customer or supplier inside a folder, not Chift's company or folder. One record carries both roles, which is why force_merge applies.
Horus requires a search key, the third-party code accountants see, that Chift does not send. The connector must generate it per folder; deriving it from the name is a Proposal (C8).
A VAT number already used by another company is refused by default. A client that already exists as a supplier must go through force_merge, not a second record.
Creation returns only an id (documented), so the response needs two to three extra read calls: company details, IBANs, and the receivable account unless cached.
There is no idempotency key and no company delete endpoint. A blind retry can leave an undeletable duplicate, so the connector searches before retrying.

not_mappable: One address per company: extra invoice or delivery addresses are lost, and later reads return one 'main' address.
No field for mobile, internal_notes, first_name, last_name, function or company_id; currency is read-only. These values are dropped and returned as null.
No company/individual flag: a client sent with is_company=false comes back as a company.
The enterprise number of a VAT-liable client has no separate field and is lost.
Non-IBAN bank accounts (local account number with routing code) cannot be stored.

horus_support: POST /daybooks.list (pick sales or purchase journals, cached)
routes.how_it_works: Horus has no endpoint that lists invoices, so each Chift invoice is rebuilt from the ledger: headers from book-entries.list (one call per sales or purchase journal, credit-note journals included) and lines, VAT, analytics and matching from one account-histories.list call. For sales, the open sales invoices list adds payment status and invoice-currency amounts; the connector then classifies, filters and paginates.
routes.documented: Pushed invoices are 'converted into book entries in the corresponding daybook' (guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices). book-entries.list returns entry headers (number, date, confirmed flag, partner, totals, attached document) for one daybook and a month period, with the partner sideloaded on request. account-histories.list returns all entry lines of a period, across several daybooks, with optional VAT, analytic, partner and matching detail. invoices.sales.outstanding.list returns open sales invoices and credit notes with open amount, payment status, transaction type and invoice-currency totals. ModifiedAfter exists on book-entries.list and account-histories.list.
depends_on_assumption: Invoice or credit note is decided by the journal type; the amount sign decides only in folders without a credit-note journal (Proposal, D1).
Ledger amounts are in EUR: foreign-currency invoices come back in EUR unless the open sales list gives the invoice currency (Proposal, D4).
Lists return the full result for the period: no paging parameter is documented, so Chift paging is emulated on a cached result.
Month periods filter on the entry date; the connector filters to the day and may widen the window by one month.
tax_code is rebuilt from the line VAT fields against the folder's accepted combinations; null when ambiguous (Proposal, D2).
reference and customer_memo are split from the header comment, whose location on read is undocumented (Proposal, D3; H9).
'paid' is inferred from full matching of the partner line, which also covers offsets by credit notes.
needs_confirmation: Horus: can the invoice/credit-note type be exposed on read, and can credit notes sit in invoice journals (H2)?
Horus: currency of ledger amounts and direction of CurrencyRate for foreign-currency invoices (H4).
Horus: limits on result size, period span, request rate and timeouts for multi-year ledger reads (H5).
Horus: does ModifiedAfter catch payments and accountant edits, and do accountant edits also create a new id (H10)?
Chift: default period without dates, unconfirmed entries returned as draft or excluded, acceptable full re-sync cadence (C10, C11).
Chift: which misclassification is more acceptable when the document type cannot be read (C5).
Chift: invoice currency while open, or one stable EUR view, for foreign-currency invoices (C16).
not_concluded: Performance on large folders: Horus documents no limits and no request was sent; to measure on a test folder.
How deleted or replaced invoices can be detected: no deletion signal is documented; webhooks are mentioned but not documented.
Whether the open sales invoices list ever returns fully paid invoices.
routes.feasibility_reason: All core invoice data is readable, but the invoice/credit-note split, foreign-currency amounts and large-folder behaviour rest on points only Horus can confirm (H2, H4, H5).

considerations.text: This is the clearest case of one Chift route needing several Horus endpoints: one header call per journal, one or two ledger calls, and the open sales list for sales types.
Updating an invoice through the API creates a new book entry with a new id. Ids stored by consumers stop working; reconcile on journal plus number.
Incremental sync (updated_after) still reads a whole month window and reports neither deletions nor replaced ids, so a periodic full re-sync is needed.
Pagination, day-level dates, payment_status and approval_status have no Horus parameter and are emulated by the connector.
There is no purchase-side open-invoice list, so purchase payments and 'paid' status come only from matching on the ledger.

not_mappable: Line quantity, unit price and unit of measure are not stored: lines return quantity 1 and unit price equal to the line amount.
delivery_date, payment_term_id, payment_method_id and withholding_tax have no per-invoice field on read and are returned null.
No 'cancelled' status and no approval workflow: approval_status stays 'unknown' unless Chift accepts Horus 'Verified' (C18).
The purchase VAT kind is not returned, so some purchase tax_codes come back null; rate and amount are still returned.
The original currency of paid sales invoices and of all purchase invoices is not readable under the EUR assumption.
Partner is_company, first name and last name are not stored: every partner is returned as a company.

routes.how_it_works: Customer invoices and refunds go to invoices.sales.new and supplier ones to invoices.purchases.new (Type 0 invoice, 1 credit note), with the PDF in the same call. Before posting, the connector resolves the journal, partner, accounts, VAT combination and analytic codes, turns analytic percentages into amounts and checks the number; after posting it reads the entry back.
routes.documented: invoices.sales.new and invoices.purchases.new create an invoice (Type 0) or credit note (Type 1) with header totals, lines (account, base, VAT amount, VAT fields), cost lines per analytic schema, currency, payment reference, comment and an optional file in the same multipart call. The posting guide lists the prerequisites: FolderId, a sales (200/250) or purchase (100/150) daybook, the CompanyId and the account search keys. Horus checks that total = base + tax and that the lines sum to the header. Only the combinations in Horus's two published tax-combination spreadsheets are valid, one list per legislation (BE, LU) and direction. Entries are unconfirmed by default for accountant review; Number is numeric and can be 0 while unconfirmed. Create returns only the book entry id, and book-entries.info reads the entry back by id.
depends_on_assumption: Each Chift tax_code is a connector-owned id for one accepted Horus VAT combination, per folder legislation and direction (Proposal, D2).
Per-plan analytic percentages become amounts on combined cost lines, assuming plans are independent; rounding keeps the exact line total (Proposal, C9).
Credit notes go in with Type 1 and positive amounts; refunds use the invoice journal when no credit-note journal exists (Proposal, D1).
VAT amounts are booked as sent (OverrideTaxAmounts = true), not recalculated by Horus (Proposal, C2).
Posting mode chosen per connection: review (unconfirmed, proposed default) or direct (status 'posted' confirmed) (Proposal, C1).
A duplicate check on the invoice number runs before creating and before any retry; best effort, since Horus documents no uniqueness rule (Proposal).
partner_info.account_number is read as the third-party code; the partner is found with a name check, otherwise created (Proposal, C8).
needs_confirmation: Horus: are the tax-combination files current and complete, which TaxOrigin list is authoritative for Luxembourg, how are invalid combinations rejected (H1)?
Horus: numbering of a confirmed invoice sent without number, uniqueness of numbers, outcome of a timed-out create (H3).
Horus: may a credit note go into an invoice journal, and are negative lines or totals accepted (H2)?
Horus: currency of the amounts sent and direction of CurrencyRate (H4); may every user set Confirmed = true (H21)?
Horus: a test licence or folder, because writes hit real data and invoices cannot be deleted (H17).
Chift: posting mode and meaning of 'draft' (C1); rule for invoices sent without number, since Horus does not number them (C7).
Chift: reject or drop inputs Horus cannot store (C3), and the meaning of partner_info.account_number (C8).
not_concluded: Effect of a mandatory free-typed analytic dimension or a locked cost section on posting (H13).
Maximum attachment size for the PDF: undocumented (H18).
routes.feasibility_reason: The native endpoints cover the route, but the VAT catalogue (H1), numbering and duplicates (H3, C7) and the posting status (C1) need answers before the design is final.

considerations.text: VAT is the main risk: Horus has no VAT-code list and accepts no code on write. Each line needs rate, origin and type, plus kind and condition for purchases.
Horus's posting guide requires the folder, daybook, partner and account codes before posting, so one Chift call needs several lookups (mostly cached) before the create.
Numbers must be numeric and invoices are not numbered automatically through the API. A number such as INV-2024/001 belongs in reference, not invoice_number.
Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default, while Chift's default status is 'posted'. The response must report the status actually stored.
No API endpoint deletes an invoice: a wrong or duplicated invoice must be corrected by the accountant, hence the duplicate check before any retry.

not_mappable: withholding_tax and nl_payment_terms_split (Dutch split payment) have no Horus field; Horus folders are Belgian or Luxembourgish. Proposal: reject with 422 (C3).
Line quantity, unit price and unit of measure are not stored: echoed in the create response, lost on later reads.
start_date, end_date, delivery_date, force_financial_period and payment_term_id have no field; the period follows the invoice date (Proposal: reject or log, C3).
reference has no own field: it shares the header comment with customer_memo and cannot be filtered on later.
Automatic numbering ('system's numbering rules') is unavailable for invoices; Proposal: an invoice without number is pushed for review and returned as draft (C7).
Currencies outside Horus's list of 32 codes plus EUR are rejected.

routes.how_it_works: One Horus call lists every daybook (journal) of the folder with its code, name, type, IBAN and currency. The connector translates the Horus daybook type into the Chift journal type and looks up the counterpart account number in the cached chart of accounts, because Horus returns only an internal reference to that account.
routes.documented: daybooks.list returns, per daybook, its Id, SearchKey (code), Heading (name), Type, Iban, currency settings and a reference to its concentration account (F). The Horus guide links daybook types 100/150, 200/250, 500, 590 and 600 to API posting endpoints (F), so these types map onto Chift journal types by deduction (D). accounts.list turns the account reference into an account number (F).
depends_on_assumption: Cash, temporary, system and cost daybooks (550, 610, 690, 700) are mapped and returned as blocked, because no API posting endpoint is documented for them.
Sales and purchase journals are returned as accepting other currencies, assuming the folder allows currencies; the API does not expose that setting.
An empty journal currency is read as 'follows the folder currency'; the daybook CurrencyCode field has no description.
Proposal: next_document_numbers stays empty by default; an estimate from the highest existing number is opt-in, as the numbering format is undocumented.
needs_confirmation: Horus: can cash or temporary daybooks receive entries through the API, and what does the daybook flag IsUsed mean (H14)?
Horus: numbering format and sequence per daybook and fiscal year (H3), only if next document numbers are required.
Chift: is an empty next_document_numbers acceptable (C4), and should non-postable journals be listed as blocked or hidden?
not_concluded: Whether a daybook can be deactivated in Horus Office: daybooks carry no status field, and the meaning of IsUsed is undocumented.
routes.feasibility_reason: The core journal fields come natively from one call; blocked, other_currencies_allowed and the type of less common daybooks rest on assumptions until Horus answers H14.

considerations.text: The Horus daybook type decides which endpoint can post entries into a journal, so it is the routing key for every write route, not only for this list.
journal_type describes the daybook, not each entry: Horus invoices carry their own invoice or credit-note type, so credit notes may sit in a sales or purchase journal.
Only bank daybooks can carry their own currency; miscellaneous, bank and financial postings have no currency field, so these journals are returned as not accepting other currencies.

not_mappable: unallocated_account: Horus exposes no suspense account per daybook or folder, so it is always empty and bank-reconciliation flows cannot prefill it.
blocked: no Horus flag; it is derived from the daybook type, so it reflects what the API can post, not settings made in Horus Office.
next_document_numbers: Horus has no numbering sequence per daybook; empty by default (the Chift default).

routes.how_it_works: The connector checks that the number is not already used, creates the account with its number and name, then reads it back, because Horus returns only an internal id. The Chift type is not sent: a Horus account has no writable type or category.
routes.documented: accounts.new takes FolderId, SearchKey (the account number) and Heading (the name) and returns only the new Id (F). accounts.info returns the stored account with its Inactive flag and category fields (F). Neither accounts.new nor accounts.update accepts a category or type (F).
depends_on_assumption: The type returned is computed from Horus data and number prefixes; a new account often comes back as 'other' or as a prefix-based guess.
The duplicate check may miss an inactive account, because whether accounts.list returns inactive accounts is undocumented.
needs_confirmation: Horus: does accounts.new derive a category from the number, and can a category be set through the API at all (H12)?
Horus: account number rules per Belgian or Luxembourg chart, and the error returned for a duplicate number (H7).
Chift: when the requested type cannot be stored, should the connector reject, warn or drop it silently (C3)?
routes.feasibility_reason: Creating an account with number and name is documented end to end; the loss of the type is itself documented, so it is a known limitation, not an uncertainty.

considerations.text: No endpoint deletes or renumbers an account, so an account created with a wrong number must be cleaned up manually in Horus Office.
The Horus search key, 'usually the account number', is how every posting endpoint references an account, so the Chift number is the join key across routes.
The Chift type sent on creation is lost: clients that classify accounts by type see a computed type, for example 'other' until a bank journal uses the account.
Horus documents no number rules (length, classes per Belgian or Luxembourg chart), so an invalid number is caught only by Horus, with an undocumented error.

not_mappable: type: Horus has no writable type or category, so the type sent is lost and the type returned may differ.
scheme_ids: Horus has no reporting-scheme classification; always empty.

horus_support: POST /account-histories.list (VAT and cash typing, filter only)
routes.how_it_works: One Horus call returns the folder's full chart (number, name, active flag, categories); the connector caches it and applies the class filter and paging itself. Horus has no account type field, so the Chift type is computed from several Horus sources and the type filter is applied to that computed value.
routes.documented: accounts.list returns SearchKey, Heading, Inactive, IntCategory, AccountCategory and AccountSubCategory per account (F); its only filters are SearchKeys ('starts with') and Heading, and it has no paging parameter (F). Bank (500) and Financial (590) daybooks reference their account (F), and ledger lines carry an account type: customer, supplier, general, VAT or cash (F).
depends_on_assumption: The type is computed from journals, categories and ledger lines; the last fallback, Belgian number prefixes, is general accounting knowledge, not Horus documentation.
type=vat and type=cash are best effort: unused VAT or cash accounts are typed only by Belgian prefixes, and not at all in Luxembourg folders.
The class filter assumes the search key is the account number, which the Horus guide says is 'usually' the case.
needs_confirmation: Horus: full list of IntCategory codes and whether AccountCategory is always filled, which would make the type reliable (H12).
Chift: when a type filter can only be estimated, return 400, ignore the filter, or return a best-effort result (C18)?
Chift: what other_expense and other_financial mean, so that Horus subcategories map to the right Chift type.
not_concluded: Whether the chart includes inactive accounts and non-postable title accounts: accounts.list has no filter for either and the documentation is silent (H12).
routes.feasibility_reason: Number, name and active status are native; the account type, which clients use to find bank, VAT or cash accounts, rests on a heuristic cascade.

considerations.text: Customers and suppliers are not separate ledger accounts in Horus: they are usually booked on shared collective accounts (e.g. 400000, 440000) with a partner reference.
Horus recommends loading the chart once and caching it per folder; with no paging in Horus, every Chift page is cut from that full list.
Bank accounts linked to a bank journal are typed reliably; VAT, cash and payable types are less reliable for accounts that have no movements yet.

not_mappable: type: no account-level field in Horus; only a computed value can be returned, which can be wrong for accounts without movements.
scheme_ids: no Horus equivalent; always empty.

routes.how_it_works: One Horus call lists every folder the connected user can access (a Horus folder is one company's books, which is the Chift folder), and Chift adds its own 'selected' flag from activation. Proposal: the address country, which needs one extra call per folder, is left empty by default.
routes.documented: folders.list returns Id, FolderName, Legislation (BE or LU), IsVatLiable, VatNumber, Address, ZipCode and Locality for the folders the user can access (F). CountryCode is returned only by folders.info (F). What a user sees through the API depends on their access in Horus (F).
depends_on_assumption: main_currency is returned as 'EUR': Horus folders have no currency field, and the base currency is assumed to be euro (H4).
active is always true for returned folders, because Horus has no folder status; a selected folder that disappears is returned as inactive.
company_number is derived from a Belgian VAT number (BE plus enterprise number), from general knowledge; empty for Luxembourg or non-VAT-liable folders.
Street and house number are split from one Horus address string, following the documented example format.
needs_confirmation: Horus: is a folder's base currency always EUR (H4)?
Horus: does folders.list return archived or closed folders, and is the enterprise number available anywhere?
Chift: is the address country needed, given that it costs one extra Horus call per folder (C4)?
routes.feasibility_reason: Id, name, VAT number and address come natively from one call; main_currency, active and company_number are assumptions because Horus folders carry no such fields.

considerations.text: A Horus folder is one company's books (the Chift folder); a Horus 'company' is a customer, supplier or beneficiary, not the legal entity.
For an accountant, the list returns every folder of the firm's license, so the activation picker may need search or filtering.
One Horus authorisation covers every folder the user can access, so Chift's folder selection at activation is what limits a connection's scope.
Each Horus license has its own API address and tokens, so one Chift connection covers one license; a firm with several licenses needs several connections.

not_mappable: Folder status: Horus has no active or archived flag; active is inferred from presence in the list.
main_currency: no Horus field; returned as 'EUR' by assumption.
Address box number: no Horus field; always empty.

routes.how_it_works: The connector posts one balanced entry into the folder's miscellaneous-operation daybook: each signed Chift amount becomes a debit or a credit, and each line type becomes customer, supplier or general. The journal, analytic codes and closure dates are looked up first, and the entry is read back only when Horus generates the number.
routes.documented: The endpoint posts an operation whose lines carry a type (1 customer, 2 supplier, 3 general), an account search key, non-negative Debit and Credit, a company id on customer and supplier lines, and optional cost lines (F). Debits and credits must balance (F). Number is numeric and can be 0 while unconfirmed; automatic numbering works only with Confirmed = true (F). API entries are unconfirmed by default, and only unconfirmed API entries can be deleted (F).
depends_on_assumption: Proposal: operations in another currency are converted to EUR at the supplied rate, because Horus operations have no currency field.
The folder currency is assumed to be EUR; Horus exposes no folder currency (H4).
operation_number is assumed to be the Horus entry number; proposal: non-numeric values and leading zeros are rejected (C7).
Proposal: a posting mode per connection; review (default) pushes every operation unconfirmed, direct confirms 'posted' operations (C1).
Only Type 600 daybooks are accepted; other miscellaneous daybook types have no documented API posting path.
needs_confirmation: Chift: does Chift core convert foreign-currency amounts before the call, in which rate direction, and how is a rounding residue absorbed (C15)?
Chift: review or direct posting by default, given Chift defaults to 'posted' and confirmed operations cannot be deleted through the API (C1).
Horus: may every licence and user type set Confirmed = true, or can some receive a 403 (H21)?
Chift: is operation_number the entry number or the client's reference; reject non-numeric values or let Horus number confirmed operations (C7)?
Horus: is the entry number unique per daybook and fiscal year, and what happens on a duplicate (H3)?
not_concluded: Whether a VAT closure also blocks miscellaneous operations: fiscal years carry both closure dates, and the guide does not say which one applies (H14).
Behaviour when a folder has several mandatory analytic plans, since Chift sends at most one analytic account per line (H13).
routes.feasibility_reason: Posting a balanced EUR operation is documented, but the status mapping (C1, H21), foreign-currency conversion (C15) and numbering (C7) need answers before the behaviour is final.

considerations.text: Horus keeps API entries unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, while Chift's default status is 'posted'; which one applies is a Chift decision (C1).
A confirmed operation cannot be deleted through the API; an unconfirmed operation pushed through the API can.
An update creates a new Horus entry with a new id, so clients should reconcile on journal and number, not on the id alone.
No idempotency key is documented, so a timed-out create is checked before any retry; this check works only when a number was supplied.

not_mappable: Original currency and exchange rate: Horus operations store EUR amounts only, so the source currency cannot be read back from Horus.
Alphanumeric operation numbers: Horus numbers are numeric, so such references cannot be stored as the entry number.

routes.how_it_works: A Horus cost schema is an analytical dimension, which is the Chift analytic plan; one call returns all of them, at most eight per folder. The connector maps each list-type schema to a plan and cuts the page itself.
routes.documented: cost-schemas.list returns Id, SearchKey, Heading, CostSectionType (List or Free) and MasterCostSchema for every schema of the folder (F). A folder can use up to 8 cost schemas (F). Analytics depend on the folder's analytics module, WithAnalytics (F).
depends_on_assumption: parent_id is taken from MasterCostSchema; whether 'master' means a parent plan is not documented.
Proposal: Free-type schemas, which have no list of values, are not returned in v1, pending Chift decision C9.
Proposal: a folder without the analytics module returns an empty list rather than an error.
needs_confirmation: Chift: should Free-type dimensions be listed or hidden, given they have no enumerable analytic accounts (C9)?
Horus: what MasterCostSchema means, and what the cost endpoints return for a folder without analytics (H13).
routes.feasibility_reason: One documented call returns every required plan field; parent_id and the Free-dimension policy are minor open points that do not affect the list itself.

considerations.text: Horus calls analytics 'cost' analytics: a plan is a cost schema (e.g. DEPARTMENT) and an analytic account is a cost section (e.g. OFFICE).
Free-type dimensions take free text, digits or dates instead of a list of values, so they do not fit Chift's plan-and-account model.
Proposal: the plan id is the Horus schema GUID; Horus posts by schema code, so invoice and operation creation translate the id through a cached lookup.

not_mappable: Plan active status: cost schemas have no active flag; always returned as active.
Plan code, description and mandatory flag: no Chift field, so users cannot see that a dimension is mandatory.

routes.how_it_works: Horus lists cost sections one schema at a time, so the connector reads the schemas first, then calls the section list once per list-type schema (at most eight) and merges the results into one Chift page. Inactive sections are requested explicitly, because the Chift route returns all analytic accounts.
routes.documented: cost-sections.list requires FolderId and CostSchemaId and returns Id, SearchKey, Heading, Inactive and the parent CostSchema for each section (F). Inactive sections are left out unless IncludeInactive is set (F). Only List-type schemas hold cost sections (F).
depends_on_assumption: Proposal: balance, credit and debit are returned empty rather than 0, because Horus stores no balance and 0 would read as a real zero (C4).
needs_confirmation: Chift: return balances empty, as 0, or computed over the current fiscal year, and on confirmed entries only or all (C4)?
Horus: is a section code unique per folder or only per plan, since the guide and the posting reference differ (H7)?
Horus: what IsLocked and IsDefault mean on a section, and whether locked sections should show as inactive (H13).
not_concluded: Computed balances: the sign of cost-history balances and the response shape are undocumented, and unconfirmed entries cannot be excluded on that endpoint.
Whether child sections appear at top level in the section list; the section hierarchy has no Chift field.
routes.feasibility_reason: Listing every analytic account of every plan is documented as a bounded loop over at most eight plans; only computed balances, if Chift wants them (C4), are not yet concluded.

considerations.text: One Chift call needs up to nine Horus calls (one schema list plus one section list per plan), so the result is cached per folder, as Horus recommends for analytics.
Horus stores no balance per analytic account; balances exist only as period totals of analytic lines, and the Chift route carries no period.
Proposal: the analytic account id is the Horus section GUID; Horus posts by code, so invoice and operation creation translate ids through the same cached list.
The section lists have no 'modified after' filter, so a section created or deactivated in Horus Office appears only after the cache refreshes.

not_mappable: balance, credit, debit: not stored per analytic account; computable only over a period the Chift route does not carry.
currency: cost sections have no currency; empty unless balances are computed, then EUR by assumption.
Section hierarchy and categories: no Chift field; the list is flattened.

routes.how_it_works: Clients: the open sales invoices list gives each open invoice or credit note with a native open amount, joined with customers.outstanding for the account and matching number. Suppliers: there is no purchase equivalent, so open items come from suppliers.outstanding ledger lines and the connector computes amount and open amount from debit and credit.
routes.documented: The guides name customers.outstanding, suppliers.outstanding and invoices.sales.outstanding.list as the open-item endpoints, and outstanding items are the lines 'not matched yet'. The sales list returns open sales invoices and credit notes with total, open amount, invoice-currency amounts, due date, payment remark, transaction type, daybook and a ConfirmedOnly filter. customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding return open ledger lines with account, daybook code, number, dates, debit, credit, matching detail and confirmed flag, but no open-amount field. Omitted filters are ignored (guide: Making requests).
depends_on_assumption: Without a company filter, the lists return the open items of every partner in the folder, complete and uncapped (H8).
Supplier open amount equals the line amount for an unmatched line; partly matched groups are netted only if Horus returns them (Proposal, D5).
Positive means owed (receivable for clients, payable for suppliers); credit notes and payments are negative (Proposal, D5).
Ledger amounts are in EUR: supplier items come back in EUR with rate 1; client items in invoice currency when given (D4).
Credit-note rows of the sales list take their sign from the transaction type, as no documented example shows a credit note.
reference is read from the partner-line comment, then entry remarks; the location is undocumented (Proposal, D3; H9).
needs_confirmation: Horus: without a company filter, do the ledger lists cover all partners, and do they return partially matched lines (H8)?
Horus: currency of ledger debit and credit, and direction of CurrencyRate (H4).
Horus: volume limits and timeouts for whole-folder open-item reads (H5); do SumDebit/SumCredit cover exactly the returned lines (H23)?
Chift: sign convention (balance or document view) and allocation inside a partly matched group (C5).
Chift: one item per due date or per invoice, and whether unallocated payments are items (C17).
Chift: should unposted payments reduce open amounts when unposted_allowed=false (C10)?
not_concluded: original_document for items carried forward from a prior year: IsReport is undefined and no link to the original document exists.
Whether the debit/credit signs in the outstanding examples are real or placeholders; the supplier example shows a debit on a supplier line.
How partially paid supplier invoices behave if Horus omits partly matched lines; a test in a test folder must choose the fallback.
routes.feasibility_reason: Client open items are native, but folder-wide completeness and supplier open amounts depend on undocumented partial-matching behaviour that Horus must confirm (H8).

considerations.text: The two sides differ: Horus gives clients a native open amount, while supplier open amounts are computed by the connector from ledger lines.
The open-item endpoints have no date, paging or modified-after filter: every request reads all open items of the folder and the connector pages them.
Entries left unconfirmed (the Horus default, and the proposed review mode) count as unposted items until the accountant confirms them, so they appear only with unposted_allowed=true.
Item ids are ledger line ids and are expected to change when the source entry is updated; consumers should re-read before matching.
Matching numbers are unique per partner, not per folder, so they must be read together with partner_id.

not_mappable: Supplier amounts in the invoice currency: ledger lines carry a currency code but no foreign amount, so items come back in EUR with rate 1 (assumption D4).
Several due dates per item and a payment method per due date: Horus has one due date per line and no readable payment method.
original_document.id for carried-forward items: no link to the prior-year document; returned null.
journal_type describes the journal, not the document: a credit note in a sales journal appears as customer_invoice; the sign tells them apart.

client.intro: On Horus, Create client becomes POST /companies.new in the Horus folder. A Chift client is a Horus "company": the one third-party record of a folder, flagged as customer and/or supplier. Most identity, contact and address fields copy across directly or with light formatting. The connector fills the Horus-required fields that Chift does not send (search key, role flags, VAT liability, language, country) by rule. Horus returns only the new id, so the Chift response is built by reading the record back.
call_flow: Reference data, cached per folder: GET /folders.info (default language and country), POST /accounts.list (checks account_number exists and is active), POST /countries.list (checks the country code).

Pre-checks with POST /companies.list (proposal): search by VAT number and by external reference, so a duplicate gets a clear Chift error or a hint to use force_merge. Then search by the generated search key to make sure the code is free in the folder.
Create with POST /companies.new: FolderId, generated SearchKey, role flags, one address, contact data and the IBANs in the same call. Horus returns only the new Id.

When force_merge is set, these calls replace step 3. GET /companies.info confirms the id is a supplier in the same folder. POST /companies.update sets IsCustomer = true. POST /ibans.new adds any IBAN not yet stored.

Read back in two to three calls. GET /companies.info gives the stored values, the last-modified date and the search key. POST /ibans.list gives the IBANs and BICs. The receivable account number comes from the cached chart, or from GET /accounts.info. One POST /companies.list call with Include might replace these calls, but that is unconfirmed (H15).
Build the Chift response from what was read back, using the same partner rules as the invoice routes (proposal): one 'main' address, is_company = true, and null for fields Horus does not store.

rows.note: Points to the Chift connection that holds one Horus licence's API address and tokens. Each Horus licence has its own database and endpoint. Not sent to Horus as data.

rows.horus_field: FolderId (companies.new body; also on every folder-scoped check)
rows.note: A Chift folder is a Horus folder ('the accounting record of one company'). If folder_id is absent, the single selected folder is used (Chift rule). With several folders and none given, the call returns 400. Who enforces the selection: C12.

rows.horus_field: CompanyId on companies.update (IsCustomer = true) + ibans.new; companies.new is skipped
rows.note: Horus keeps customer and supplier in one record, so the existing supplier is flagged as customer instead of duplicated. Proposal: check it is a supplier in this folder, fill only empty fields, never overwrite its VAT number or reference (C6).
Same meaning, required on both sides. Also the basis for the generated search key (proposal). Horus documents no maximum length.
Horus recommends this field for your own identifier, so the company can be found again reliably. Proposal: also use it for the duplicate check. Whether Horus keeps it unique is undocumented (H7).
Horus has no company/individual flag: every third party is a 'company' record. Business impact: an individual is stored as a company and comes back as one.

A Horus company has no person-name fields. The FirstName/LastName on beneficiaries are for payroll payees and must not be used. Proposal option: put first + last name in ContactPerson, whose meaning is to confirm (H11).
Not stored, same as first_name. An individual's name survives only inside name.
Horus has no job-title field. The value is dropped, so the client application must keep it.
Horus has no link from a person to a parent company. Proposal: ignore the value, or reject it if Chift prefers strict behaviour (C3).

The ISO code is upper-cased (fr → FR). The Horus company list is FR, NL, DE, EN, ES, PT, XX. Proposal: any other value, or none, gets the folder language because Horus requires one. The original value is then lost.
Proposal: active = false sets CustomerActivitySuspended = true. Horus gives this field no description, so its meaning must be confirmed before relying on it (H11).

Same number, and IsVatLiable = true when it is present. By default Horus refuses a VAT number already used. Proposal: clean or reject dots and spaces (C20), and check for duplicates first to return a clear error.

Horus has no field to write it. It returns EnterpriseNumber only for companies that are not VAT-liable. Hypothesis: send it as VatNumber with IsVatLiable = false (to confirm, H11). Otherwise the value is lost.

Both mean the receivable account. Horus takes the number itself, so no id lookup is needed. Proposal: check it exists and is active in the cached chart. The default when omitted is undocumented (H11).
A client currency cannot be set. Horus sets currency per invoice. Business impact: the client's default currency is not stored.
Copied. Horus seems to return it as ContactPhone on read: same data under another name, deduced from the field names (to verify, H25).
A Horus company has no mobile field (only folders do). Proposal option: use it as PhoneNumber when phone is empty. Otherwise it is dropped.
Copied to the general contact e-mail. Horus also has InvoiceEmail and ReminderEmail. Copying email into those too is optional (proposal).
Copied. Seems to come back as ContactWebsite on read (deduced from the field names, to verify, H25).
A Horus company has no notes field. The value is dropped, so the client application must keep its notes.

rows.note: Spaces are removed and the IBAN is marked as the default account. Horus fills in the BIC automatically. Proposal: check the IBAN checksum and reject an invalid IBAN with 422 (C20).

rows.note: Horus keeps one address per company. Proposal: keep main, else invoice, else delivery, and drop the others (C3). Chift allows an empty list; the folder country is then used.
Horus addresses have no type. The value only decides which address is written, and the address always comes back as 'main'.
One line: street + number (+ box), as in the Horus example 'Quai des Ardennes 9'.
Merged into the address line. It cannot be split back out reliably, so it is returned as null.
Proposal: append it to the address line as '/box'. Address2 exists, but its meaning is undocumented (H11).
Copied.
Copied.
Upper-cased two-letter ISO code (two letters is deduced from the 'BE' examples), checked against the cached Horus country list. Proposal: reject an unknown code with 422.
Horus has no per-address name. Name2 exists, but its meaning is undocumented, so it is not used.
Proposal: use it only when the root phone is empty, otherwise drop it.
No mobile field, so it is dropped.
Proposal: the invoice address's e-mail fills InvoiceEmail. The main address's e-mail fills ContactEmail only if email is empty. A delivery e-mail is dropped.

rows.horus_field: Id from the companies.new response (with force_merge: the supplier's Id)
rows.note: The Horus company id, and the only value the create call returns. Later invoices for this client must reference it as CompanyId.
Not in the create response, so it needs the read-back call.
Returns the search key the connector generated, which is the client's code as accountants see it in Horus.

rows.note: On read, Horus returns a reference to the account, not its number, so it must be resolved. Null if Horus applies no default (undocumented).

rows.note: One entry per stored IBAN. is_primary marks the main IBAN. bic_swift is the BIC as Horus filled it. currency, account_number and routing_code are always null.
iban is the main IBAN stored. bank_account is null, because Horus stores IBANs only.
Proposal (same partner rule as the invoice routes): always true, because Horus does not store the flag. A client sent as an individual comes back as a company.
Proposal: always exactly one 'main' address, with number, box, name, phone, mobile and email null. A client sent without an address comes back with one that holds only the folder country.
Lower-cased. Proposal: Horus 'XX', whose meaning is undocumented, comes back as null. A language that fell back to the folder default comes back as that default.
Proposal: active = not suspended, and true when the field is absent. Depends on what the Horus field means (H11).
Filled only for companies that are not VAT-liable. A VAT-liable client returns null, even when a number was sent.
The value Horus holds, not the request value. For companies, the docs do not say whether an empty value means EUR.

rows.note: Always null, because Horus does not store them. A later Get clients call returns the same.

rows.chift_field: All other fields (name, vat, external_reference, phone, email, website)

Proposal: format errors (VAT, country, IBAN) return 422 before Horus is called. Duplicates and unknown references return 400 with the Horus Details. Horus documents one error type only ('not_found'), so the mapping is partial (C20, H6).

horus_required_extra.how_filled: Proposal: generated from the name (upper-case, letters and digits only, shortened), with a number added if the code is taken, after checking it is free in the folder. Horus documents that the key is unique within the folder, but not its length or allowed characters (H7). The convention needs Chift's agreement (C8).
Always true, because the route creates a client.
Always false on creation. With force_merge, the existing supplier keeps true and gains IsCustomer = true.
Derived: true when a VAT number is sent. Risk: a VAT-registered client sent without its number is stored as not VAT-liable.
From language. Proposal: the folder language (folders.info) when language is missing or outside the Horus list.
From the chosen address. Proposal: the folder country (folders.info) when addresses is empty, which may be wrong for the client.

horus_required_extra.horus_field: FolderId (companies.new and every folder-scoped check, required)
horus_required_extra.how_filled: From folder_id. If it is absent, the single folder selected at Chift activation (Chift rule). If there are several folders, the call returns 400.

horus_required_extra.horus_field: CompanyId / Id on the follow-up calls (companies.info, companies.update, ibans.list, ibans.new)
horus_required_extra.how_filled: Taken from the companies.new response, or from the force_merge value.

key_points.text: A Chift client is a Horus 'company': the single third-party record of a Horus folder, flagged as customer and/or supplier. One record holds both roles, which is why force_merge maps cleanly: the existing supplier is flagged as customer instead of being duplicated.

One Chift call needs several Horus calls. Horus create calls return only an id, so the company, its IBANs and (unless cached) its receivable account are read back to build the Chift response. That is two to three extra calls, and about three to seven in total with the checks. Rate limits are undocumented (H5).

Horus requires a search key, role flags, a VAT-liability flag, a language and a country that Chift may not send. The search key is the main business choice, because it becomes the client's code that accountants see. Proposal: generate it from the name. The convention is to agree with Chift (C8) once Horus states the rules (H7).

Some data cannot be stored: extra addresses, mobile, notes, person fields, job title, company link, client currency, non-IBAN bank accounts, and the enterprise number of VAT-liable clients. Individuals come back as companies. Client applications must keep this data on their side. Whether to reject or drop such input is a Chift decision (C3).

Duplicates: by default Horus refuses a VAT number that is already used, and it documents no idempotency key. Proposal: search by VAT number and external reference before creating, and never retry blindly after a timeout. Without either value there is no reliable duplicate check (C8).

Open before build: the merge policy (C6), the error codes (C20), the meaning of the 'suspended' flag used for active (H11), and a test folder (H17). Writes go to real data, and the API has no call to delete a company.

client.coverage_check: Checked against appendix_chift_spec_extract.md (POST /consumers/{consumer_id}/accounting/clients), not only against create_client.json. Path and query parameters: consumer_id, folder_id and force_merge each have a row. ClientItemIn: all 21 attributes have a row each (external_reference, first_name, last_name, name, function, is_company, company_id, phone, mobile, email, language, internal_notes, website, vat, company_number, iban, bank_account, currency, active, addresses, account_number). AddressItemIn: all 11 attributes have a row each (address_type, name, number, box, phone, mobile, email, street, city, postal_code, country). Response (ClientItemOut, AddressItemOut, BankAccountsItem, RoutingCodeItem): only fields that are not a plain read-back of the request get their own row (id, last_updated_on, third_party_account, account_number, is_company, language, active, company_number, currency). Deliberately grouped: the bank_accounts[] subfields in one row; the deprecated iban and bank_account in one row; the AddressItemOut subfields in one row; the six fields always returned as null in one row; name, vat, external_reference, phone, email and website in one 'read back from Horus' row. A ChiftError row covers the 400/422 responses the contract declares. Chift error-code names that appear in create_client.json are left out, because they are not in the spec extract.

invoice.intro: On Horus, a Chift sale or purchase entry becomes a book entry created by invoices.sales.new (customer invoices and refunds) or invoices.purchases.new (supplier invoices and refunds), with the PDF in the same call. Most header and line amounts map directly. The work is in four areas: resolving references (folder, daybook, company, accounts, analytic dimensions), turning each Chift tax code into a Horus VAT combination, converting analytic percentages into amounts, and deciding what to do with Chift fields that Horus cannot store.
call_flow: Reference data, cached per folder: daybooks.list to pick or check the sales/purchase daybook, accounts.list to check line accounts, cost-schemas.list and cost-sections.list to turn analytic ids into the search keys Horus posts with, and folders.info for the folder legislation (BE/LU), which selects the VAT list. fiscal-years.list is read fresh before each create, because the accountant can close a period at any time.

Partner: companies.info checks that partner_id belongs to the folder and has the customer or supplier role. Without partner_id, companies.list finds the company from partner_info and companies.new creates it if it is missing (proposal). Horus needs a CompanyId before it accepts an invoice.

Duplicate check: book-entries.list filtered on the document number. Horus has no idempotency key and the API has no invoice delete, so this check runs before the create and before any retry (proposal, best effort).
Create: invoices.sales.new for customer_* or invoices.purchases.new for supplier_*, with the PDF in the same multipart call. Horus returns only the new entry Id.

Read-back, skipped when ignore_accounting_id=true: book-entries.info by Id gives the stored number, confirmation status and last-update date. account-histories.list is added only when line-level data is needed, such as the EUR amount of a foreign-currency invoice or the partner's collective account.

rows.note: Identifies the Chift connection, which holds the Horus licence URL and tokens. Never sent to Horus.
Same id as Get folders; Horus needs it on every call. Proposal: if empty, use the only folder selected at activation, otherwise reject (folder question C12).
No Horus field sets the accounting period of an invoice. Proposal: accept only when it equals the invoice-date month, otherwise reject (period questions H10, C3).
The connector merges lines with the same account, tax code and analytics before posting. Nothing is lost: Horus lines hold no quantity or price anyway.
Horus returns the id immediately, so it is always available. true only skips the read-back; stored status and last-update date are then not confirmed.
true: send currency_exchange_rate as CurrencyRate. false: send none and Horus applies its rate of the day (which day is undocumented, currency question H4). Ignored for EUR.
customer_* → sales endpoint, supplier_* → purchase endpoint; invoice → Type 0, refund → Type 1. Also selects the daybook type and the VAT list.
Proposal: Horus numbers are numeric, so non-numeric or leading-zero values are rejected (the printed number goes in reference). No number: push unconfirmed with Number 0 (numbering questions C7, H3).
Same id as Get journals; must be a sales (200/250) or purchase (100/150) daybook of the folder. If empty, the single matching daybook is used, otherwise error.
Proposal: posting mode per connection. Review (default): always unconfirmed, for accountant review. Direct: posted → confirmed. Response shows the stored status (posting questions C1, H21).
Date → date-time with offset. As Horus recommends, the connector first checks that the date is in an open fiscal year, after the accountant's closure dates.
Date → date-time. Horus holds one due date per invoice, so instalments cannot be expressed.
No delivery or tax-point date in Horus. Same month as invoice_date: no impact. Other month: VAT period may differ; reject or accept is Chift's call (C3, H10).
No accrual or deferral period on Horus invoices; the accountant must book the deferral manually. Proposal: ignore and log, or reject (unsupported-inputs question C3).
Same as start_date: no Horus field; the accountant books the deferral manually. Proposal: ignore and log, or reject (C3).
EUR → empty (the Horus default). 32 other ISO codes are accepted, only if the folder is configured for currencies; any other code is rejected.
Sent only when force_currency_exchange is true and currency is not EUR. Rate direction (1 EUR = x or the reverse) is undocumented on both sides (H4).
Same meaning; Horus checks that the line bases add up to it. For foreign currency, whether Horus reads amounts in that currency or in EUR is undocumented (H4).
Same meaning; line taxes must add up to it. Proposal: OverrideTaxAmounts=true so Horus keeps the invoiced VAT instead of recalculating base × rate (VAT question C2).
Horus rejects an invoice unless total = untaxed + tax; the connector checks this before calling.
Copied as is, e.g. the Belgian structured communication +++040/7139/58328+++. Maximum length undocumented.
Proposal: Chift id = Horus payment-mode code from its fixed list (0 Bank Transfer, 110 Domiciliation, 200 Credit Card…). Convention to agree with Chift.
Horus invoices have no payment term. No real loss: due_date is mandatory and is sent. Ignored.
Dutch G/N split: Horus folders are Belgian or Luxembourg only and invoices have no split field. Proposal: reject the whole object (C3).
Rejected with nl_payment_terms_split; Horus invoices carry no IBAN.
Rejected with nl_payment_terms_split (no Horus equivalent).
Rejected with nl_payment_terms_split; Horus invoices carry no IBAN.
Horus has no field for an external or supplier invoice number. Proposal: stored in the header comment as 'reference | memo'. Impact: not searchable, cannot serve duplicate checks.
Proposal: shares the header comment with reference. The comment length limit is undocumented, and where Horus returns the comment on read is unconfirmed (H9).
Same id as Create/Get clients and suppliers. Proposal: also check it belongs to the folder and has the customer or supplier role (Horus behaviour undocumented, H11).
Proposal: only when partner_id is empty: find the company by code, check its name, else create it. Recommended path: create the client first (partner_info question C8).
Proposal: not described in Chift's spec; read as the third-party code, not a ledger account (to confirm, C8). Used exactly as sent; codes Horus would not accept are rejected.
Name of a company created from partner_info. Also compared with a found company's name to avoid booking to the wrong partner (proposal).
Horus invoices have no withholding tax. Proposal: reject the invoice rather than book wrong totals (unsupported-inputs question C3).
Rejected with withholding_tax (no Horus field).
Rejected with withholding_tax. Impact: an invoice carrying withholding tax cannot be pushed to Horus as such.
One Horus line per Chift line, or per merged group when regroup_lines is on. Horus lines are accounting lines: account, amounts, VAT, analytics.
Used only to order lines; Horus has no line-number input.
Copied as the line comment. Maximum length undocumented.
Horus posts on the account search key (e.g. 700000), i.e. the account number. Proposal: checked first against the cached chart of accounts (exists, active).
Same meaning; also the base for analytic amounts. Line bases must add up to the header untaxed_amount (Horus rule).
Same meaning; must add up to the header tax. Kept exactly only with OverrideTaxAmounts=true (proposal, C2); otherwise Horus may adjust it within 1 cent.
Validation only (= untaxed + tax). Horus lines have no total; nothing is lost.
Horus invoice lines hold no price or quantity; used only to check amounts. Impact: lost in Horus; invoice retrieval would return quantity 1 and unit price = line amount (proposal, C4).
Not stored (see unit_price). Impact: quantity is lost in Horus and reads back as 1.
Not stored; ignored. Impact: the unit is lost in Horus.

rows.horus_field: InvoiceLines[].TaxRate, TaxOrigin, TaxType (+ TaxKind, TaxCondition, TaxConditionValue on purchases; TaxCountryCode on OSS sales)
rows.note: Proposal: Horus takes no VAT code, only field combinations listed in its BE/LU files. A connector-owned VAT-code list decodes each code; unknown codes are rejected (C2, H1).
Same unit (21 = 21 %). The connector checks it matches the rate inside the tax code.
No shipping country on Horus invoices. OSS lines take the country from the tax code; shipping_country only cross-checks it (proposal). No impact otherwise.

Proposal: Horus stores amounts on combinations of dimensions, not percentages per plan; multi-plan splits are combined assuming plans are independent (C9). Max 8 dimensions; folder needs analytics enabled.
Chift plan id = Horus cost schema id; posting needs its search key, read from the cached schema list. Proposal: Free-type schemas not accepted in v1 (C9).
Chift account id = Horus cost section id; posting needs its search key from the cached list. Proposal: inactive or wrong-plan sections rejected.
Amount = line base × percentage(s), rounded so cost lines add up exactly to the line base (Horus rule). Impact: small lines may read back with slightly different percentages.
Proposal: if header and lines differ by rounding within an agreed tolerance, add a correction line so Horus's sum checks pass; larger gaps rejected (tolerance question C19).
Decoded through the sales VAT list, like lines[].tax_code. Needed only when a sales correction line is generated.

rows.horus_field: Correction line TaxRate, TaxOrigin, TaxType, TaxKind, TaxCondition, TaxConditionValue
rows.note: Decoded through the purchase VAT list. Needed only when a purchase correction line is generated.
Account number of the sales correction line (Horus account search key).
Account number of the purchase correction line (Horus account search key).
Base64 decoded and sent with the invoice in one call. Accepted types: PDF, XML, CODA, SODA, JPG, PNG. Size limit undocumented (H18).
Horus requires a file name with extension when a file is attached. Proposal: a default name when pdf_name is missing.
Horus returns only the new book-entry id. Impact: an invoice update creates a new entry with a new id; Horus advises reconciling on daybook + number.
Number as stored; 0 (no number) is returned as empty. Whether Horus numbers an invoice when the accountant confirms it is undocumented (H3).
Status actually stored: confirmed → posted, unconfirmed → draft. In review mode a 'posted' request comes back as 'draft' (proposal, C1).
Ids actually used, including a company found or created from partner_info and an auto-selected daybook.
Needs the read-back call; empty when ignore_accounting_id is true.
Assumption: 'EUR'. Horus folders expose no currency field and an empty currency means EUR. To confirm with Horus (H4).
Assumption: for a EUR invoice it equals total. For foreign currency, the EUR amount is read from the ledger lines (extra call), assuming ledger amounts are in EUR (H4).
Customer or supplier collective account (e.g. 400000) read from the ledger lines; needs an extra call, empty without it.
'yes_to_request' when a PDF was sent (Horus serves files as bytes, not URLs; fetched via the attachments route), otherwise 'no'. Attachment list empty.
Always one element (due date, total, payment method), because Horus holds a single due date per invoice.
Empty: a newly created invoice has no matched payments.
'unknown': no approval workflow at creation (Horus Verified is false by default).
Empty by default: this route has no include_partner_info parameter. One extra company call could fill it if Chift wants it.
Lines as booked: merged lines when regroup_lines is on, plus any correction line. tax_code, percentages, quantity and unit price are echoed, not read from Horus.
Returned empty: Horus does not store them.

rows.chift_field: Other response fields (invoice_type, currency, amounts, dates, reference, customer_memo, payment fields)

Picked from daybooks.list by invoice type: sale 200, sale credit note 250, purchase 100, purchase credit note 150. Exactly one daybook must match, otherwise error, as Chift's contract describes. Proposal: when the folder has no credit-note daybook, a refund falls back to the invoice daybook; Horus has not confirmed it accepts this (H2).
Proposal: found or created from partner_info (C8). With neither partner_id nor partner_info, the invoice is rejected.

Proposal: decoded from lines[].tax_code through the connector's VAT-code list, built from Horus's accepted-combination files for the folder's legislation (BE/LU) and direction. Horus must confirm the files are current and complete (H1).

horus_required_extra.how_filled: Proposal: decoded from the same tax_code. These fields are part of the accepted combination even where the schema marks them optional.
Line base × the analytic percentage(s), rounded so the cost lines add up exactly to the line base, as Horus requires. The rounding method (largest remainder) is a proposal.

horus_required_extra.horus_field: FileName (required when a file is attached)
horus_required_extra.how_filled: pdf_name with its extension. Proposal: a default '<number or id>.pdf' when pdf_name is missing.

horus_required_extra.horus_field: companies.new required fields in the partner_info flow: IsCustomer, IsSupplier, IsVatLiable, LanguageCode, CountryCode
horus_required_extra.how_filled: Proposal: role from invoice_type, IsVatLiable=false, and the folder's language and country. Impact: the company has no VAT number or address and must be completed in Horus.

horus_required_extra.horus_field: OverrideTaxAmounts (optional, but decides how VAT is booked)
horus_required_extra.how_filled: Proposal: always true, so the invoiced VAT is kept. The Horus default recalculates base × rate and adapts the amount within 1 cent; behaviour beyond 1 cent is undocumented (C2, H22).
Left empty, since Chift has no source. Whether Horus refuses a line on an account that requires a vehicle is undocumented and should be asked.

key_points.text: One Chift call becomes several Horus calls. Before posting, Horus needs the folder, the daybook, the company and the search keys of accounts and analytic dimensions. Its create call returns only an id, so the Chift response is rebuilt from the request plus a read-back.

VAT is the main gap. Chift sends one tax_code per line, but Horus accepts no VAT code: it takes a combination of rate, origin and type (plus three purchase fields), valid only as listed in Horus's BE/LU spreadsheets. Proposal: a connector-owned VAT-code list per folder. Horus must confirm the files are current (H1), and Chift must accept the approach (C2).

Posting status and numbering need Chift decisions. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, while Chift defaults to 'posted'. Horus invoice numbers are numeric, and invoices have no automatic-numbering option. Proposal: review mode by default, and Number 0 (returned as draft) when no number is sent (C1, C7).

Some fields cannot be mapped: withholding tax, the Dutch G/N split, accrual dates, a forced period or a delivery date in another month, payment terms, and line quantity, unit price and unit. reference survives only inside the comment. Rejecting these inputs or silently dropping them is a Chift product decision (C3), because the create response has no warnings field.

Analytics change shape. Per-plan percentages must become amounts on combinations of up to 8 dimensions. Multi-plan splits assume the plans are independent (C9), and small lines may read back with slightly different percentages.

There is no undo. The API has no invoice delete, and an update creates a new entry with a new id, so a duplicate or wrong invoice cannot be removed through the integration. Hence the number check before any retry (best effort) and the need for a test folder during development (H17).

invoice.coverage_check: A script extracted every path and query parameter and every request attribute of this operation from appendix_chift_spec_extract.md and matched them against the row names, with nothing missing. That covers 6 parameters (consumer_id, folder_id, force_financial_period, regroup_lines, ignore_accounting_id, force_currency_exchange), the 28 top-level attributes of InvoiceItemInMultiAnalyticPlans, and 29 nested leaf attributes: WithholdingTax 3, InvoiceCorrection 4, NlPaymentTermsSplit/PaymentTermAccountInfo 4, AccountToCreate 2, InvoiceLineItemInMultiAnalyticPlans 12, AnalyticDistribution 2, AnalyticDistributionDetail 2. Some containers are grouped on purpose: withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split (with g_account and n_account) and analytic_accounts[] are covered by their leaf rows. invoice_correction, partner_info, lines[] and analytic_distribution keep their own rows because the object itself drives a mapping. For nested fields, 'required' means required within the optional parent object, as in the Chift spec. On the response side, only fields that are not simply echoed get a row. The rest sits in the 'Other response fields' row and in two grouped rows (partner_id + journal_id; payment_term_id + delivery_date + withholding_tax).

outst.intro: The route returns the open (unpaid or unallocated) items of a folder's customers or suppliers. Horus has open-item lists for both sides, but they are not symmetric. Client items come from the open sales invoices list, which has a native open amount, joined with customer ledger lines. Supplier items are rebuilt by the connector from supplier ledger lines. Each Chift item is therefore assembled from two or three Horus sources, and the connector or Chift handles signs, currency and paging.
call_flow: POST /daybooks.list (cached per folder): gives each journal's id, code and type. This feeds journal_id and journal_type, because supplier lines carry only the journal code.

type=client: POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list for the whole folder (ConfirmedOnly when unposted_allowed=false). Returns open sales invoices, credit notes and linked payments with open amount, due date, invoice-currency amounts and payment remark.

type=client, in parallel: POST /customers.outstanding with no company filter. Returns customer ledger lines, joined on the line id to add account number, matching number and line comment. An open sales row missing from this list triggers GET /account-histories.info (fallback).
type=supplier: POST /suppliers.outstanding with no company filter. Returns supplier ledger lines; the connector computes amount and open amount (Credit − Debit) and filters on Confirmed itself.

Chift side: drop linked payments that Horus lists twice, apply filters, sort, return the requested page and count the total. Optional, off by default (Proposal): GET /book-entries.info per entry for the supplier payment communication and carried-forward details.

rows.note: Identifies the Chift connection. Chift uses it to find the stored Horus licence URL and tokens. Nothing is sent to Horus.
Horus documents no paging, so Chift fetches the full open-item set, sorts it and returns the requested page. Speed on large folders is unverified (H5).
Page size of the emulated pagination (default 50). It does not change the Horus calls, which always return the whole set.
Same concept: a Horus folder is the accounting record of one company. If omitted, the single folder selected at activation is used, as Chift's own folder rule states.
Chooses the Horus endpoints. Clients need two lists (open sales invoices plus customer ledger lines); suppliers have only ledger lines. Employee open items are not covered.
false keeps only accountant-confirmed entries: a native filter on the sales list, a connector filter on ledger lines. Whether unconfirmed payments still reduce open amounts depends on C10.
Proposal: one item per open customer or supplier ledger line. A linked payment that Horus lists twice is kept once. Instalments and unallocated payments are open questions (C17).
Computed by Chift: number of items after filtering and de-duplication, counted on the full set fetched from Horus.
Echo of the requested page.
Echo of the requested page size.
The ledger line id, the unit that Horus matching works on. Not stable: updating the source invoice creates a new entry, so the id presumably changes.
Converted to text. 0 (an unconfirmed entry without a number) becomes null. Numbers are unique only within a journal, so read them together with journal_id.
Clients: the daybook id is on the row. Suppliers: Horus gives only the journal code, so the id is looked up in the cached daybook list.

rows.horus_field: Type (daybooks.list), reached through the item's daybook
rows.note: Proposal: a shared daybook-type table (sale → customer_invoice, sale credit note → customer_refund, bank → financial_operation…). It describes the journal, so a credit note keyed in a sales journal reads customer_invoice (H2).
Date part of the Horus date-time, with no time-zone conversion. Preferred over AccountingMonth/AccountingYear; Horus describes neither field.
Date-time converted to a date. On the sales list Horus fills it only for invoices and credit notes, so payments come back with null.
Horus has one due date per ledger line, so the list has zero or one element. Several instalments become several items (question C17).
Same value as items[].due_date.

rows.horus_field: — (invoice PaymentMode can be written but not read)
rows.note: Returned null. Horus accepts a payment mode when an invoice is created, but no read endpoint returns it, so payment apps cannot see the expected payment method.
Returned null, for the same reason as payment_method.
Proposal: equals open_amount (remaining amount due), since each item has one due date. Use amount instead if Chift means the scheduled instalment amount.
Proposal: open sales invoices keep their own currency. Supplier and other ledger lines are returned in EUR, because Horus gives no foreign-currency amount for them. Depends on H4 and C16.

rows.horus_field: TotalAmount / TotalCurrencyAmount (invoices.sales.outstanding.list); constant 1 for EUR items
rows.note: Proposal: 1 for every euro item. For foreign-currency sales rows, computed from the two amounts Horus returns. The direction of Horus's own CurrencyRate is undocumented (H4).

rows.horus_field: TotalAmount / TotalCurrencyAmount (invoices.sales.outstanding.list); Debit − Credit (customer lines); Credit − Debit (suppliers.outstanding)
rows.note: Proposal: positive = owed (invoice +, credit note and payment −). Horus documents no sign rule: clients are signed from the transaction type, suppliers use Credit − Debit. Depends on C5 and H2.

rows.horus_field: OpenAmount / OpenCurrencyAmount (invoices.sales.outstanding.list); computed from Debit, Credit, MatchDetail (suppliers.outstanding)
rows.note: Clients: documented Horus open amount. Suppliers: Horus has no open amount, so the line amount of unmatched lines is used. Partially paid supplier invoices depend on H8 (Proposal: net per matching group).
Horus company id, Horus's term for a customer or supplier. A line without a counterparty cannot be returned because partner_id is required (Proposal: skip and log it).

rows.horus_field: AccountSearchKey (customers.outstanding, joined on line id; suppliers.outstanding)
rows.note: Suppliers: on the line. Clients: the sales list has no account, so it comes from the joined customer ledger line. Horus search keys are 'usually the account number'.
One-element list when matched, otherwise empty. Horus appears to number matchings per customer or supplier, so values are unique only with partner_id (question C17).
Horus 'confirmed by the accountant' is read as Chift 'posted'; the sources do not equate the two. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default.

Proposal: the first non-empty value of the ledger-line comment, then the sales remark, keeping the part before ' | ' (invoice-creation convention). Where Horus shows the invoice comment is undocumented (H9).
Clients: Horus payment remark (e.g. a structured communication). Suppliers: not on the supplier list, so null in v1. Proposal: an optional per-entry read, off by default.
Meant for items carried forward from an earlier year. Horus flags such lines (IsReport) but does not define the flag. Proposal: null in v1 until Horus explains it (H8).
Horus documents no link from a carried-forward line to the prior-year line. Always null, so consumers cannot trace the original item by id.
Only if original_document is filled: the carried-forward line's number, assuming it keeps the original one. Null if the line sits in an opening entry (H8).
Same assumption: the carried-forward line's journal, looked up in the cached daybook list. Null if it is a technical opening journal (H8).
Same daybook-type table as items[].journal_type. Null when original_document.journal_id is null.
Date part, assuming the carried-forward line keeps the original document date (H8).
Date part or null, under the same assumption (H8).
Same rule as items[].reference, applied to the carried-forward line (H9, H8).

horus_required_extra.how_filled: From folder_id. If folder_id is omitted, the single folder selected at activation is used (Chift's own folder rule). With several selected folders, the request is rejected with 'folder_id required'.
Proposal: constant 0 ('All folders'). Used only when folder_id is omitted and no folder selection is stored for the connection, to find the single folder the user can access.
The line id of an open sales row that is missing from the customer ledger list. Used to read that row's account number and matching number.
Proposal, off by default: the book entry id of a supplier or carried-forward line, to read its payment remark and entry type. One cached call per distinct entry.

key_points.text: Clients and suppliers are built differently. Clients get Horus's documented open amount. Horus has no open-amount list for suppliers, so the connector uses the amount of unmatched ledger lines. Whether partially paid supplier invoices appear at all depends on Horus (H8, a priority-1 question). If they do not, a fallback is needed that reads unmatched ledger lines over a period.

One Chift call needs several Horus calls. Clients take two (the open sales list plus customer ledger lines, joined on the line id) and suppliers take one, plus a cached daybook list for journal ids and types. No loop per partner is needed, provided that leaving out the company filter returns the whole folder (to confirm, H8).

Horus documents no paging, so Chift fetches the full open-item set and pages it itself. Response time on large folders is unverified (H5), and keeping a short cache between page calls needs Chift's agreement (C14).

Not mappable or degraded: payment_method (Horus does not return it on read), original_document (carry-forward flag undefined; null in v1, Proposal), at most one due date per item, and supplier payment_communication (null by default). Horus credit-control data (reminder level, payment status, cash discount) has no Chift field. Item ids are expected to change when the source invoice is updated.

Signs and currency are connector proposals that still need agreement. Positive means owed, so credit notes and payments are negative (C5, H2). Open sales invoices keep their own currency and every other line comes back in EUR, so one customer's items can mix currencies (C16, H4).

With unposted_allowed=false, only entries confirmed by the accountant are returned. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default, so they stay out of that view until the accountant confirms them. Whether the connector can push them as confirmed is the posting-mode decision (C1).

outst.coverage_check: Checked against the Chift spec extract for GET /consumers/{consumer_id}/accounting/outstandings: 1 path parameter (consumer_id) plus 5 query parameters (page, size, folder_id, type, unposted_allowed); the ChiftPage envelope (items, total, page, size); the 18 OutstandingItem fields; the 4 OutstandingItemDueDatesOut fields; and the 7 OriginalOutstandingItem fields. That makes 39 rows, one per attribute, with none grouped, and matches the 39 field_mappings in data/outstandings.json. The extract does not list the enum values of OutstandingType or BoolParam, so 'client/supplier' and 'true/false' follow the route name and the analysis. One claim in the data file was softened: that a linked payment is returned both inside the invoice and as its own row. The appendix shows top-level payment rows and LinkedElements, but not the raw duplicated example, so the claim is stated as a deduction.

differences.chift: Client and supplier are separate resources. A client can be an individual (first_name, last_name, is_company = false) and carries several typed addresses (main, delivery, invoice), plus mobile, internal notes and currency fields.
differences.horus: Each third party is one 'company' record, flagged IsCustomer and/or IsSupplier. companies.new requires SearchKey (unique within the folder), Name, IsVatLiable, LanguageCode and CountryCode. It holds one address (Address, Address2, ZipCode, Locality) and has no person, mobile or notes fields.
differences.why_it_matters: Client creation has to generate a search key that Chift never sends and derive VAT liability, language and country. force_merge becomes 'add the customer flag to the existing supplier'. Extra addresses, person fields and is_company are lost, and every partner reads back as a company.
