differences.chift: A journal has a journal_type (customer_invoice, customer_refund, supplier_invoice, supplier_refund, financial_operation, miscellaneous_operation, unknown). On an entry, invoice_type gives the document kind.
differences.horus: A daybook has a numeric Type, and that Type decides the posting endpoint: 200/250 sales and sales credit notes, 100/150 purchases and purchase credit notes, 600 miscellaneous operations. No posting endpoint is documented for cash, temporary, system, budget or external daybooks. Invoice vs credit note is a separate Type 0/1 on the invoice.
differences.why_it_matters: Invoice and operation creation must pick the daybook from invoice_type (proposal: the credit-note daybook, with a fallback). Invoice retrieval must read both sibling daybook types. journal_type describes the daybook, not every entry in it.

differences.chift: tax_code is required on every invoice line. It is the id of a VAT code in the accounting software, and GET vat-codes lists those codes.
differences.horus: Horus has no VAT-code list endpoint and accepts no VAT code on write. Each line carries TaxRate, TaxOrigin and TaxType (purchases add TaxKind, TaxCondition and TaxConditionValue), and only the combinations in two published spreadsheets, one per direction, each with a BE and an LU sheet, are valid. On read, lines return VatCode/VatHeading strings whose meaning is undocumented, and no TaxKind.
differences.why_it_matters: The connector has to own a VAT-code catalogue per folder legislation and direction, with synthetic ids decoded on write and encoded on read. Some purchase lines cannot be matched to a single code on read, so their tax_code comes back null.

differences.chift: Invoices and outstanding items are documents: a header, lines, type, payments, due dates and open amount.
differences.horus: Posted invoices become book entries (headers, listed per daybook and month period) and account-history lines (lines, VAT, analytics, matching). The only document-level list is invoices.sales.outstanding.list: open sales invoices and credit notes, with OpenAmount. Purchases have no equivalent, and book entries do not say whether they are an invoice or a credit note.
differences.why_it_matters: Invoice retrieval has to be rebuilt from several endpoints, and telling invoices from credit notes on read rests on an assumption. Client open amounts are native, but supplier open amounts must be computed by the connector from unmatched ledger lines.

differences.chift: For each line and each plan, whole-number percentages that add up to 100 % per plan. Miscellaneous operations take one analytic account per line.
differences.horus: Cost lines are amounts allocated to combinations of cost sections (one value per cost schema) and must add up exactly to the line base amount. A folder has at most 8 cost schemas. Free-type schemas (900) have no listable sections.
differences.why_it_matters: A converter has to turn independent per-plan percentages into amounts on combinations and back (proposal: product of percentages, largest-remainder rounding). Small amounts can read back with a different split. Free-type dimensions are hidden in v1 (proposal, C9).

differences.chift: status defaults to 'posted'. invoice_number and operation_number are free strings; when missing, they are generated 'according to the system's numbering rules', and they are recommended for idempotency.
differences.horus: Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default (Confirmed = false) so the accountant can review them. Number is numeric, required, and may be 0 only while the entry is unconfirmed. Automatic numbering (AutoGenerateNumber, confirmed entries only) exists for miscellaneous, bank and financial operations, not for invoices.
differences.why_it_matters: Chift's default 'posted' collides with Horus's review-by-default design, so the connector needs a posting-mode rule. It cannot confirm an invoice sent without a number. Non-numeric numbers must be rejected or moved to reference.

differences.chift: A create call returns the full object with a stable id, and consumers reconcile by that id.
differences.horus: Creation returns only {Id}. Every invoice or operation update creates a new book-entry Id (full replacement; the original attachment is deleted). No idempotency key is documented, and there is no delete endpoint for invoices, companies or accounts.
differences.why_it_matters: Write routes need a read-back to build the Chift response, and a best-effort duplicate check before every create and before any retry. An invoice id changes after an edit, so consumers must reconcile on journal and number.

differences.chift: Lists are paginated (page, size, total) and filtered by day-level date_from/date_to, updated_after and type.
differences.horus: No list request has paging parameters. Ledger reads take month periods (StartMonth, StartYear, EndMonth, EndYear). ModifiedAfter exists only on companies.list, book-entries.list and account-histories.list. No deletion signal is documented.
differences.why_it_matters: The connector fetches full results and emulates paging, totals and day-level filters. That lists return complete results is a deduction, unverified on large folders (H5). The design needs a cache between page calls (C14) and a periodic full re-sync to catch deletions and replaced ids.

differences.chift: A consumer connection with folders selected at activation. folder_id is required when several folders are enabled, and requests to unselected folders must be rejected.
differences.horus: Each license (accounting firm or SMB) has its own database and API URL, returned at the end of OAuth, and the user picks one license. What the API shows depends on that user's access in Horus. Almost every call needs a FolderId, but calls by Id take none.
differences.why_it_matters: The api_url must be stored per connection. One grant covers every folder the user can access (deduction), so either the connector or Chift's platform (C12) must enforce the selected folders and check the folder on Id-only calls.

limitations.title: VAT codes exist only as published tax combinations
limitations.what: Horus accepts no VAT code on write and has no VAT-code list. A line is valid only if its rate, origin and type (plus kind and condition on purchases) match a combination listed in two spreadsheets, each with a BE and an LU sheet (F). The TaxOrigin enums in the API reference miss the Luxembourg codes used in the files, and TaxKind is not returned on read (F).
limitations.implication: GET vat-codes and every tax_code become connector-owned data. Luxembourg folders and folders that are not VAT liable remain uncertain. Some purchase VAT codes come back empty on read. If the files are incomplete, codes that clients need cannot be posted.
limitations.handling: Proposal: build the catalogue from the files, with one list per folder legislation (BE/LU) and direction and one synthetic id grammar (D2). Reject a code outside the folder's list with 422 before calling Horus. Return tax_code = null on read when the match is ambiguous. Book VAT as sent (OverrideTaxAmounts = true, D16). Descoping trigger: a reduced VAT-code list if needed codes cannot be expressed.
limitations.decision_owner: Both: Horus confirms that the files are current and which origin list is authoritative (H1); Chift accepts the synthetic catalogue and the VAT-amount policy (C2).
limitations.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes (dependency)

limitations.title: 'Posted' and numbering do not map one to one
limitations.what: Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default, for accountant review. Number is numeric, required, and may be 0 only while the entry is unconfirmed, and invoices have no automatic numbering (F). Whether every licence and user type may set Confirmed = true is not documented (?).
limitations.implication: A request with Chift's default status 'posted' may come back as 'draft'. An invoice to be confirmed without an invoice_number cannot be posted as confirmed. Numbers such as INV-2024/001 are rejected. An entry pushed without a number cannot be found again after an accountant edit.
limitations.handling: Proposal: a posting mode chosen per connection, either review (default; Confirmed = false) or direct ('posted' sent as Confirmed = true). The response always reports the status actually stored. An invoice without a number is pushed for review and returned as a draft. Non-numeric numbers are rejected with 422, and the number shown to customers goes in reference.
limitations.decision_owner: Chift decides (C1, C7); Horus confirms confirmation rights and numbering behaviour (H21, H3).
limitations.routes: Invoice creation, miscellaneous operation creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items

limitations.title: No documented paging, limits or timeouts
limitations.what: No Horus list request has paging parameters, ledger reads are bounded by month, and no rate, size or time limit is documented (F: the documentation is silent). That lists return complete result sets is a deduction (D).
limitations.implication: Unless results are cached between calls, every Chift page may re-read the full period. Behaviour on large accounting-firm folders, including any silent truncation, is unverified. Incremental reads filter headers, but ledger lines are still read per period, so polls stay costly.
limitations.handling: Proposal: a per-folder reference cache plus a short-lived result cache (subject to C14); a bounded default window for invoice retrieval (current fiscal year, C11); a volume test on the largest test folder as the exit criterion of phase 1. Descoping trigger: a mandatory date window or journal filter on invoice retrieval.
limitations.decision_owner: Both: Horus states its limits (H5); Chift decides on caching, timeouts and default windows (C14, C11).
limitations.routes: All list routes; most exposed: invoice retrieval, outstanding items

limitations.title: Invoices are rebuilt from the ledger, without the document type
limitations.what: There is no general invoice list. Headers come from book-entries.list per daybook and period, lines from account-histories.list, and neither exposes invoice vs credit note (F). TransactionType exists only on open sales items (F).
limitations.implication: This is the most complex read route, with several Horus calls per request. A credit note keyed into the sales daybook of a folder that also has a credit-note daybook comes back as an invoice with negative amounts. Line quantity and unit price are not stored, so on read a line has quantity 1 (proposal).
limitations.handling: Proposal: the daybook type decides; the sign of the partner line is used only in folders without a credit-note daybook; TransactionType is a consistency check, not an override (D1). The rule stays labelled as an assumption until Horus exposes the type.
limitations.decision_owner: Both: Horus on credit-note rules and the type on read (H2); Chift chooses which misclassification is acceptable (C5).
limitations.routes: Invoice retrieval; also outstanding items and journals

limitations.title: Supplier open amounts are computed, not read
limitations.what: Client open items come with a native OpenAmount from invoices.sales.outstanding.list (F). Suppliers have only ledger lines (suppliers.outstanding). Two points are undocumented (?): whether partially matched lines are returned, and whether every partner is returned when CompanyIds is omitted.
limitations.implication: Payables are complete only if Horus returns partially matched lines, or if a fallback read is used. Otherwise every supplier balance can silently drop partially paid invoices, and this is a Task B route.
limitations.handling: Proposal: open amount = Credit − Debit of each unmatched line. Partially matched groups are netted if Horus returns them (remainder allocated oldest due date first, C5). Fallback: read the supplier concentration accounts with account-histories.list. Control check against Horus's SumDebit/SumCredit. First test case: one partially paid purchase invoice and one partially paid sales invoice.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus on completeness and partial matching (H8); Chift on sign, allocation and item granularity (C5, C17).

limitations.title: No idempotency key, and ids change on update
limitations.what: A create returns only an Id, and no idempotency key is documented. Invoice and operation updates create a new book-entry Id. Invoices, companies and accounts have no delete endpoint (F).
limitations.implication: A timeout on create can lead to a duplicate that cannot be deleted. Every create response needs a read-back. Ids kept by client applications stop working after an edit, and an entry pushed without a number has no business key to find it again.
limitations.handling: Proposal: search before every create (VAT number, external reference, account number, document number) and never retry blindly. When the record has no key, return an 'outcome unknown' error. Consumers reconcile on journal and number, and should always send a number.
limitations.decision_owner: Chift on the duplicate policy and errors (C6, C7); Horus on duplicate numbers and commits after a timeout (H3).

limitations.title: Currency support differs by object
limitations.what: Invoices accept CurrencyCode and CurrencyRate when the folder allows currencies, but miscellaneous-operation lines have no currency field (F). The currency of ledger amounts on read is not documented, and invoice-currency amounts appear only on open sales items (F).
limitations.implication: Foreign-currency operations are stored in euro and lose their original currency. On read, a foreign-currency sales invoice may switch from its own currency to euro once paid, and purchase invoices always come back in euro.
limitations.handling: Proposal: never pair euro amounts with a foreign currency code (D4). Convert foreign-currency operations at the supplied rate, as Chift's contract describes, with the rate required; who converts is C15. Verify with one foreign-currency invoice in the test folder. Chift may prefer one stable euro view (C16).
limitations.decision_owner: Both: Horus on the currency of ledger amounts (H4); Chift on conversion and representation (C15, C16).
limitations.routes: Miscellaneous operation creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items, invoice creation (response)

limitations.title: Third-party master data is narrower than Chift's client
limitations.what: companies.new requires SearchKey, IsVatLiable, LanguageCode and CountryCode; beyond 'unique within the folder', the search-key rules are undocumented. A company holds one address and no person, mobile or notes fields, and a second company with the same VAT number is created only when AllowDuplicateVatNumber is true (default false) (F).
limitations.implication: The connector invents the customer code that accountants see. Extra addresses and person fields are lost. Duplicate handling must be defined for VAT matches and for clients without a VAT number or external reference.
limitations.handling: Proposal: generate the search key from the name (uppercase, accents removed, truncated, numeric suffix on collision, D10). Keep the main address, else the invoice address. Run a duplicate pre-check that returns 'already exists' with the existing id, and use force_merge for existing suppliers. Apply the same rules to partner_info.
limitations.decision_owner: Chift (C8, C3, C6); Horus on search-key rules and field meanings (H7, H11).
limitations.routes: Client creation (Task B), invoice creation (partner_info), supplier creation (dependency)

limitations.title: Testing runs on real data
limitations.what: Requests run against the license's real database; write tests need a test license or test folder, and no sandbox is documented (F). The registration and Quickstart pages were not in the reviewed documentation (?).
limitations.implication: None of the assumptions can be checked before Horus provides a test license: VAT acceptance, credit notes, partial matching, currency and volumes. Test invoices and companies cannot be deleted through the API.
limitations.handling: Proposal: Gate 0 before build: register the integration, obtain a test license and folder, and run a volume test. Descoping trigger: no build without a test license.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus provides access (H17, H19); Chift makes the go decision.

questions.question: Tax combinations: (a) Are the two published spreadsheets current and complete for BE and LU folders, and how are changes announced? (b) Which TaxOrigin list is authoritative, given that the LU files use origins outside the API reference enums, and does the API accept those codes? (c) Which combination does a folder that is not VAT liable send, and is PCT sent as 35 or as 0.35? (d) How is an invalid combination rejected? (e) Are VatCode and VatHeading on read stable, and does each correspond to exactly one combination?
questions.why: Decides whether the connector's VAT catalogue can serve every tax_code clients send, and whether purchase VAT codes can be returned on read. A negative answer triggers a reduced VAT-code list.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

questions.question: Credit notes: Can a credit note (Type 1) be posted in a 200/100 daybook, and an invoice in a 250/150 daybook? Can the invoice type be exposed on book-entries.list or account-histories.list? Must credit-note amounts be positive, and are negative lines or totals accepted on Type 0?
questions.why: Decides daybook selection and the sign rules on write, and the invoice/credit-note classification on read, which today is an assumption.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, journals, outstanding items

questions.question: Numbering and duplicates: Is Number unique per daybook and fiscal year, and is a duplicate rejected (with which error)? Is there an idempotency key, or an external reference that could serve as one? Can a create that timed out still be committed, and is a new entry listed as soon as the call returns? What happens to a confirmed invoice sent with Number 0, and could invoices get AutoGenerateNumber?
questions.why: Decides whether duplicate checks and retries are safe, and whether confirmed invoices sent without a number can be supported.

questions.question: Currency: For foreign-currency documents, in which currency are ledger Debit/Credit and book-entry totals expressed? In which direction is CurrencyRate given, and is the folder base currency always EUR? Does invoices.*.new read amounts in the invoice currency?
questions.why: If ledger amounts are in the document currency, the EUR assumption (D4) returns wrong amounts on every foreign-currency read.
questions.routes: Invoice retrieval, outstanding items, invoice creation, miscellaneous operations

questions.question: Volumes: Are there rate limits, timeouts, maximum result sizes or maximum period spans on list endpoints? Can a list result be truncated without warning?
questions.why: Paging is emulated over full results. The design is unverified on large accounting-firm folders, and silent truncation would corrupt Chift totals.

questions.question: Outstanding items: With CompanyIds omitted, do customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding return every partner's open lines, without a cap? Are partially matched lines (MatchStatus 0) returned, with every line of the group, and are Debit/Credit the original amounts or the open remainder? How is a carried-forward line linked to its original document?
questions.why: Decides whether supplier outstanding items, which the connector computes, are complete, and which call pattern the route uses.

questions.question: Confirmation rights: May every integration, licence and user type set Confirmed = true on invoices and operations, or can the accounting firm restrict it? Which actions are blocked once an entry is confirmed? Are unconfirmed entries included in balances and VAT returns?
questions.why: Decides whether the proposed direct posting mode (Chift 'posted' sent as confirmed) can be offered on every connection, and what 'draft' means for clients.

questions.question: Onboarding: (a) Is docs.horus-software.be authoritative, and is the apiary documentation linked in the case deprecated? (b) How is an integration registered (client id and secret, redirect URIs), and which user should authorise it for an accounting firm and for an SMB? (c) Can Chift get a test license or test folder, and can test data be removed? (d) What happens to tokens when the authorising user leaves or authorises again?
questions.why: Every mapping rests on the current documentation, and the two versions were not compared. Nothing can be verified or built safely without a registered integration and a test license.

questions.question: Posting mode and numbering: (a) Should the connector offer a posting mode per connection: review (entries pushed unconfirmed, proposed default) or direct ('posted' sent as confirmed), with the response always reporting the stored status? (b) An invoice without invoice_number: push it for review as a draft (proposed), reject it, or let the connector generate the next number? (c) Is rejecting non-numeric numbers acceptable, with the number shown to customers kept in reference?
questions.why: Chift's default 'posted' and free-text numbers collide with Horus's review-by-default design and numeric-only numbers. The answers fix the invoice and operation creation mappings and what clients see.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, miscellaneous operation creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items

questions.question: Caching and timeouts: Can a connector keep a per-folder reference cache and a short-lived result cache between page calls of the same request? What is the timeout of a synchronous request, and is there a background pattern for heavy reads?
questions.why: Without a cache between page calls, every Chift page re-reads the whole Horus period. This decides whether emulated paging is viable.

questions.question: Foreign-currency miscellaneous operations: Does Chift core convert the amounts to the journal currency before calling the connector, as the other_currencies_allowed description suggests, or must the connector convert? In which direction is the rate expressed, and how should a rounding residue be absorbed?
questions.why: Horus operation lines have no currency field. The answer decides where conversion happens and what the operation response returns.

questions.question: Signs: Do consumers send refund amounts as positive values, and can invoices have negative lines or a negative total? On outstanding items, should a customer credit note or an unallocated payment be negative (balance view, proposed) or positive (document view, as in invoice due dates)?
questions.why: Changes the sign rule in invoice creation and the amount mapping of outstanding items (both Task B). Without a decision, the same credit note is positive in invoice retrieval and negative in outstanding items.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items

questions.question: VAT codes: Is a connector-owned catalogue with synthetic ids (for example S-21-0-0), one per folder legislation and direction, acceptable for GET vat-codes, with tax_code = null on read when the match is ambiguous? Should VAT amounts be booked as sent (OverrideTaxAmounts = true, proposed) rather than recalculated by Horus within one cent?
questions.why: Fixes the tax_code mapping of invoice creation (Task B) and the VAT-amount policy, since Horus has no VAT-code entity.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

questions.question: Partner codes: How should the Horus search key of a new client be generated: from the name (proposed), from external_reference, or with a per-consumer scheme? What does partner_info.account_number mean, a third-party code or a ledger account? When a code matches a partner with a different name, should the connector refuse (409) or reuse it with a warning?
questions.why: Horus requires SearchKey, Chift has no field for it, and accountants see the code. The Chift spec does not describe partner_info.account_number. Changes the client creation and invoice creation mappings (Task B); the Horus search-key rules (H7) constrain the answer.

confirmed.text: Every object in scope has a documented Horus endpoint for the operation the case needs: companies.new/info/list (clients); invoices.sales.new and invoices.purchases.new, optionally with the PDF (invoice creation); book-entries.list and account-histories.list (invoice retrieval); daybooks.list (journals); accounts.new and accounts.list (ledger accounts, chart of accounts); folders.list (folders); book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new (miscellaneous operations); cost-schemas.list and cost-sections.list (analytics); customers.outstanding, suppliers.outstanding and invoices.sales.outstanding.list (outstanding items).

What is established is feasibility at capability level. No route lacks a Horus capability in the documentation reviewed, so the reference's headline holds only with the qualifier 'blocked by a missing capability in the documentation reviewed'. Applying the verdict definitions strictly gives 1 Supported route (folders) and 10 Supported with workaround. On current evidence, the open questions can degrade behaviour or narrow scope (Luxembourg VAT codes, direct posting, large folders) but do not remove a route.

The write-side rules are documented, so the connector can check them before posting. Invoice total = base + tax, and the lines add up to the header. Cost lines add up to the line base amount. Miscellaneous operations must balance. Type 0/1 marks invoice or credit note. Confirmed is false by default, Number may be 0 only while unconfirmed, and AutoGenerateNumber works only on confirmed operations.

The accepted VAT combinations are published in two spreadsheets linked from the invoice reference pages, downloaded 13 Oct 2026: sales 18 BE and 58 LU rows, purchases 109 BE and 146 LU rows. folders.list returns each folder's legislation (BE/LU), so a per-folder catalogue can be built.
confirmed.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

confirmed.text: Client open items are native. invoices.sales.outstanding.list returns a folder's open sales invoices and credit notes with OpenAmount, PaymentStatus and TransactionType, and can be filtered by company.

The connection mechanics are documented: an OAuth authorisation code flow with one license per grant, an api_url per license, one-hour access tokens and single-use refresh tokens. ModifiedAfter exists on companies.list, book-entries.list and account-histories.list, and updated invoices and operations get a new Id.

assumption.text: Emulated paging, totals and day-level filters are correct only if Horus lists return complete result sets for a folder and period. This is deduced from the absence of paging parameters and is unverified on large folders.
Invoice/credit-note classification on read is a proposed rule, not documented behaviour: the daybook type decides, and the partner-line sign is used only in folders without a credit-note daybook.
Ledger amounts on read are in the folder currency (EUR). Open sales items returning TotalAmount next to TotalCurrencyAmount suggest this, but no source states it.
assumption.routes: Invoice retrieval, outstanding items, invoice creation (response)

assumption.text: Supplier outstanding items: suppliers.outstanding without CompanyIds returns every supplier, and partially matched lines are either returned or covered by a fallback read of the supplier accounts.
The spreadsheets are current and complete, and the API accepts the Luxembourg TaxOrigin codes that the reference enums omit.
assumption.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

assumption.text: Analytic combinations are derived as the product of independent per-plan percentages, with largest-remainder rounding.

Field meanings used in the mapping are assumed. active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended. The invoice header Comment carries reference and customer_memo and comes back on read in the partner-line comment or a remark field (D3).
assumption.routes: Client creation, invoice creation, invoice retrieval

confirmation.text: Horus, VAT: the spreadsheets are current and complete, which origin list is authoritative, the combination for folders that are not VAT liable, and how an invalid combination is rejected (H1).
confirmation.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

confirmation.text: Horus, posting: whether a credit note may sit in a sales or purchase daybook and whether the type can be read (H2); duplicate-number behaviour, commits after a timeout and numbering of confirmed invoices (H3); whether every licence and user may confirm entries (H21).
confirmation.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, miscellaneous operation creation

confirmation.text: Horus, reads: the currency of ledger amounts and the direction of CurrencyRate (H4); rate, size and time limits (H5); completeness and partial matching of the outstanding endpoints (H8).
confirmation.routes: Invoice retrieval, outstanding items, all list routes

confirmation.text: Horus, onboarding: which documentation is authoritative (the case links the former apiary documentation), integration registration, the authorising user, and a test license or folder (H17 and new questions).
Chift, architecture: the posting mode and the rule for invoices without a number (C1, C7), caching between page calls and request timeouts (C14), and who converts foreign-currency operations (C15).
confirmation.routes: Invoice creation, miscellaneous operation creation, all list routes

confirmation.text: Chift, Task B conventions: input and output signs (C5), acceptance of a synthetic VAT catalogue and the VAT-amount policy (C2), and partner-code generation and the meaning of partner_info (C8). Also needed: confirmation that the contract used (OpenAPI bundled in the chift 0.6.16 SDK) matches docs.chift.eu.
confirmation.routes: Client creation, invoice creation, outstanding items

not_concluded.text: Whether the routes perform and stay correct on large accounting-firm folders. No limits are documented and no volume test has been run, so the reference's claim that the connector 'can absorb' the workarounds is not established.
not_concluded.routes: All list routes, especially invoice retrieval and outstanding items

not_concluded.text: Whether supplier outstanding items are complete for partially paid invoices. This depends on H8, or on the fallback being validated on test data.
Whether Chift's 'posted' can be delivered on every connection. Confirmation rights are undocumented (H21); if confirmation is restricted, entries come back as drafts.

Whether every VAT case clients need can be expressed. The files have no variant for folders that are not VAT liable, Luxembourg uses origins outside the reference enums, and the format of the PCT value is ambiguous.

Whether incremental synchronisation is complete. It is undocumented whether matching changes or accountant edits update ModifiedAfter, and whether an edit in Horus Office creates a new Id; no deletion signal is documented (H10).

Whether the mapping holds for the API version the case links (apiary) and for the live Chift contract. The analysis used docs.horus-software.be and the SDK-bundled Chift spec, and sent no request to a Horus license or a Chift environment.

corrections.reference_said: Section 1 (Executive summary): "All eleven Chift routes in scope can be built on the Horus Software API, and none is blocked. Two map almost directly (folders and analytic plans). Nine need workarounds that the connector can absorb, at the cost of extra calls, emulated behaviour, or data loss...". Tiles: "2 Supported / 9 Supported with workaround / 0 Not supported / 0 To confirm". Section 6 building block: "Horus lists return everything."
corrections.now: Lede: "No route is blocked by a missing Horus capability in the documentation reviewed." The split is computed from the data: 1 Supported (folders), 10 Supported with workaround, 0 Not supported. The "To confirm" tile is replaced by "4 routes waiting on a priority-1 answer": invoice creation (H1, H3, C1, C7), invoice retrieval (H2, H4, H5), outstanding items (H8, H5) and miscellaneous operations (C1, C15). Complexity spread: Low for folders, analytic plans, journals and analytic accounts; Medium for client creation, ledger account creation, chart of accounts and misc operations; High for invoice creation, invoice retrieval and outstanding items. Volume wording becomes: "expected to work for typical folder sizes; behaviour on large folders is unverified (H5)". "Lists return everything" is labelled D (a deduction from the absence of paging parameters).
corrections.why: The reference's own H1 said "Invoice creation cannot post valid VAT without them", which contradicts an unqualified "none is blocked". Horus documents no size or rate limits: the reference's own large-folder row in section 7 is "To confirm", so "can absorb" had no evidence behind it. No Horus list schema in appendix_horus_api_reference.md has paging parameters, so "returns everything" is inferred, not stated. The corrected build tiles read 1 / 10 / 0 / 4.

corrections.topic: Verdict scale applied strictly; analytic plans downgraded; new rating columns
corrections.reference_said: Section 2 "How to read": "Supported One native Horus endpoint, plus cached reference data, serves the route with deterministic transformations. Losses are limited to minor optional fields." and "To confirm The documentation is insufficient to decide." Section 4 overview: "Analytic plans retrieval ... POST /cost-schemas.list | List | Supported"; folders: "GET /folders.info (country, optional) | List | Supported".
corrections.now: The definitions are applied with no exceptions (D11). Supported: native endpoint(s), deterministic mapping and cached lookups only, with no extra live calls per request, no emulated filtering, paging or numbering, and no lost capability. Supported with workaround: feasible, but needs extra live calls, emulation, or loses a capability. To confirm: feasibility itself depends on an unanswered question. Analytic plans becomes Supported with workaround (Low complexity; impact "Minor: free dimensions hidden"). Folders stays Supported only because folders.info (country) is no longer called by default (C4). New columns on the section 4 overview: build complexity, client impact and depends on (priority-1 questions), explained in a rating note. Complexity and impact are the analyst's assessment, to calibrate with Chift.
corrections.why: Chift Get analytic plans is paginated (appendix_chift_spec_extract.md › GET analytic-plans: "param[query] page: integer default=1", response "ChiftPage_AnalyticPlanItem_"), while cost-schemas.list has no paging, so page, size and total are emulated (D). Free-type schemas ("`900`: Free" in cost-schemas.list) are hidden by design pending C9 (A). Get folders returns "array[FolderItem]" (unpaginated), so it needs no emulation (F). The reference's own workaround definition ("emulated filters, pagination or numbering") already covered analytic plans.

corrections.topic: Tax-combination spreadsheets: available and analysed (not missing)
corrections.reference_said: Section 2 Sources: "Not available | Quickstart, integration registration, support/FAQ and changelog pages; the accepted tax-combination spreadsheets; the Postman collection; webhook documentation | Points that depend on them are marked “To confirm”." H1: "Can you share the accepted tax-combination files for sales and purchases?" Task B lines[].tax_code: "built from the Horus accepted-combination files (not provided; requested from Horus)".
corrections.now: Both spreadsheets are linked from the Horus reference. They were downloaded on 13 Oct 2026 and analysed in a new appendix C. Sales: BE 18 rows, LU 58. Purchases: BE 109 rows, LU 146. Each file also has an "Available values" sheet. The VAT-code catalogue is built from these files. H1 (tier 1) changes from "send us the files" to: confirm they are current and complete, say how changes are announced, and say how an invalid combination is rejected (status and ErrorType). Gate 0 includes this confirmation. Every "not provided / requested from Horus" statement goes. The sentence "Points that depend on them are marked To confirm" is dropped, because no row carried that label.
corrections.why: appendix_horus_api_reference.md › invoices.sales.new/update: "The accepted tax combinations (Tax rate / origin and type) are available [here](…Tax-combinations-sales.xlsx)"; invoices.purchases.new/update: "The accepted tax combinations (Tax type / kind / rate / origin / condition / condition value)) are available [here](…Tax-combinations-purchases.xlsx)". The row counts are the sheet headers in appendix_horus_tax_combinations.md. Asking Horus for files its own reference links would signal an incomplete source review.

corrections.topic: VAT catalogue per folder legislation and direction; documentation discrepancies
corrections.reference_said: Appendix B D2: "S-{rate}-{origin}-{type} for sales (plus -{country} for OSS lines, origin 13), P-{rate}-{origin}-{type}-{kind}-{condition}-{condition value} for purchases". One catalogue serves every folder. Task B evidence for tax_code cites "TaxOrigin *: number enum[0..20]".
corrections.now: There is one list per folder legislation (BE or LU, from folders.list/info) and per direction (sales list for customer_*, purchase list for supplier_*). GET vat-codes becomes folder-scoped. A tax_code is valid only if it is in that list (otherwise 422). Validation uses the files, never the reference TaxOrigin enums, and labels come from the files. The country component applies to every OSS row: BE origin 13, and LU origins 24, 26 and 29, whose rate and country are "XX" (supplied per transaction). Discrepancies flagged to Horus in H1(b)(c): (a) the sales TaxOrigin enum stops at 20, but LU sales use origins up to 35; the purchase enum stops at 39, but LU purchases use 40–56. (b) Some codes have different labels: sales 16 is "Ventes Art 44" in the reference and "Ventes d'immobilisés" in the file; purchases 12 is "Hors CEE sans facture" in the reference and "Achat TVA Marge" in the file. (c) TaxCountryCode is described as "Only used for OSS Vat lines (TaxOrigin = 13)". (d) PCT is 35/50/75/85 in the combinations but 0.35… in "Available values". (e) Typo "Nationam". Folders that are not VAT liable have no variant in the files; this becomes an H1 sub-question.
corrections.why: appendix_horus_api_reference.md › invoices.sales.new: "TaxOrigin *: number enum[0, …, 20]" and "TaxCountryCode … // Only used for OSS Vat lines (TaxOrigin = 13)"; invoices.purchases.new: "enum[0, …, 39]" and "`12`: Hors CEE sans facture". appendix_horus_tax_combinations.md: "LU | 1 | European | XX | 26 | XX | (OSS) UE - Ventes Marchandises - distance", "BE | 0 | Nationam | 0 | MERCH | 0 | … | 12 | Achat TVA Marge", and Available values "35 | 0.35". As written, the reference mapping would reject or mislabel valid Luxembourg lines.

corrections.topic: Foreign-currency miscellaneous operations: converted, not rejected
corrections.reference_said: Section 7: "Miscellaneous operations: the request has no currency field, so non-EUR operations are rejected (derived; proposed default, see C3)." Section 1 data-loss list: "miscellaneous operations are EUR-only". C3 lists "non-EUR operations" under "reject or ignore with a warning?". Misc-op card: "non-EUR operations (no currency field) ... cannot be posted".
corrections.now: Proposal: a non-EUR operation is converted at the supplied rate. It is never rejected and never posted unconverted. currency_exchange_rate is required when currency ≠ EUR, and 1 counts as missing because it is the Chift default. Who converts is a new tier-1 Chift question (C15). The preferred reading is that Chift core converts before calling the connector. The fallback is that the connector converts line by line, rounds to 2 decimals, and returns 422 if rounding unbalances the entry, unless Chift defines a residue rule. The balance check uses the same normalised amounts that are sent. Amounts are stored in EUR and the original currency is not kept (it may be noted in the line comment). The response never pairs EUR amounts with a foreign code (D4). "Non-EUR operations" is removed from C3.
corrections.why: Chift contract (appendix_chift_spec_extract.md › JournalItem.other_currencies_allowed): "If it doesn't allow other currencies an exchange rate must be provided for Chift to convert the amounts to the journal currency". Misc-op currency_exchange_rate: "Must be filled in when creating the operation in another currency from the folder's default currency." The Horus misc-op body has only "Debit *: number // Non-negative amount" / "Credit *" and no currency field (F), so amounts are stored in the folder currency (EUR assumed, H4). Rejecting contradicts Chift's own text, and "ignore with a warning" would book foreign amounts as EUR.

corrections.topic: Posting status default (Chift 'posted' vs Horus Confirmed)
corrections.reference_said: Section 3 concept map: "Posted / draft | Confirmed true / false | API entries are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them before confirming. | Documented". Appendix B D12: "“draft” → unconfirmed; “posted” → confirmed, with a per-consumer option to always push unconfirmed."
corrections.now: Proposal (decision owner Chift, C1, tier 1): a posting mode chosen per connection at activation. Review mode is the proposed default: every entry is pushed with Confirmed = false for the accountant to confirm. Direct mode sends "posted" as Confirmed = true and "draft" as false. The response always reports the status actually stored, so a "posted" request in review mode comes back as "draft". The posted = Confirmed pairing is labelled D/A, not Documented. On Horus, Chift "draft" means booked, visible in default list reads, not yet confirmed by the accountant, and still deletable through the API for misc operations. Whether every licence or user may set Confirmed = true is undocumented (new H21, tier 1). Consequences: review mode gives no AutoGenerateNumber; direct mode makes confirmed misc operations undeletable, needs a non-zero number on confirmed sales invoices, and may return a 403.
corrections.why: Horus guide › Data model: "Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default ( Confirmed: false ), which lets the accountant review them in Horus Office before confirming them. Some operations, such as deleting a miscellaneous operation, are only possible on unconfirmed entries." Guide › Reading accounting data: "By default, lists include unconfirmed entries". Chift: status default="posted" ("posted (finalized) in the accounting system"). No source equates the two. The 72 endpoints have no invoice delete (only book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.delete). Under the reference default, every request sent with Chift's default status would skip the accountant's review.

corrections.topic: Recommendation: conditional go with a gate and phases
corrections.reference_said: Section 1: "Recommendation Proceed with a Horus connector covering all eleven routes, built on a small set of shared components... Before building, settle the open questions with Horus that change the design, mainly the tax-combination files, credit-note daybooks, document numbering, the currency of ledger amounts and rate limits, and get a test license". Section 9: "None of these needs changes on the Horus side, but a handful of answers from Horus would remove the main assumptions."
corrections.now: "Go, conditional on a short gate" (a proposal, not a commitment by Chift or Horus). Gate 0: integration registration (H19), a test licence and test folder (H17), Horus confirmation that the tax files are current (H1), volumes, rate limits and timeouts (H5), and Chift decisions on posting mode (C1) and numbering (C7). Phase 1: reference reads plus client and ledger-account creation, with a volume test on the largest test folder. Phase 2: invoice creation and misc operations (VAT catalogue, numbering, duplicate and timeout scenarios). Phase 3: the ledger-rebuilt reads (invoice retrieval, outstanding items) once H2, H4, H5 and H8 are answered. Descoping triggers: a reduced VAT list, a mandatory date window or journal filter on invoice retrieval, and no build without a test licence. Questions now carry tiers (1 before build, 2 route design, 3 verifiable in a test folder). New ids: H19–H25 and C14–C20; existing ids are unchanged.
corrections.why: Horus has no sandbox (reference section 3: "Requests run against the license’s real database... no sandbox is documented"). Limits are undocumented (H5). Posting and numbering are client-visible decisions owned by Chift (C1, C7). An ungated "proceed" over-commits on all three. Review issues S1-03 and S1-09, lead decision LD4.

corrections.reference_said: Section 6 building block: "Duplicate protection | Search before create (VAT number, external reference, document number) and check before retrying after a timeout or server error, because Horus has no idempotency key." Section 7: "Never retry blindly. Search for the record first (external reference, VAT number, document number) and re-post only if it does not exist. | All write routes | Derived".
corrections.now: Renamed "Best-effort duplicate protection". Search-then-retry works only when the record has a key. Some records have none: an invoice or operation sent without a number, an operation numbered by Horus, or a client without a VAT number or external reference. These are never retried automatically, and the connector returns an explicit "outcome unknown" error (C6). Supplier invoices without a number get a heuristic check on supplier, date and total (configurable, C6). Identical in-flight calls are serialised by a connector-side lock (proposal). Consumers are advised to always send invoice_number, operation_number and external_reference. H3(b) asks whether a timed-out create can still commit and whether a new entry is listed immediately.
corrections.why: Horus guide › Responses & errors gives only "500 : retry later with exponential backoff". No idempotency key appears among the 72 endpoints, and the docs say nothing about commit-after-timeout or read-after-write. Sales Number "can be 0 if not confirmed" and purchase Number is "Nullable", so unnumbered entries leave nothing to search on. Chift contract: invoice_number "is recommended to use this number for idempotency to prevent duplicate entries." Invoices cannot be deleted through the API, so a duplicate falls to the accountant to fix.

corrections.topic: Supplier open amounts and partial matching
corrections.reference_said: Section 4 card and section 5 Task B summary: "Supplier items come from supplier ledger lines, with the open amount computed from matching groups." Section 7: "Partial payments and instalments. | Open amounts come from matching groups." H8 asks only about scope without CompanyIds, carried-over lines and a purchase-side open list. Section 9: "supplier outstanding items computed from matching".
corrections.now: Supplier open_amount = Credit − Debit of each unmatched line, so the line is open for its full amount (D). Netting per (company, MatchNo) group, with the remainder allocated oldest due date first, applies only if Horus also returns partially matched lines (A; the allocation rule is a proposal to Chift). H8 is now tier 1 and blocks this route. It adds: are partial lines returned, and with their whole group? Are Debit and Credit the original amounts or the open remainder? Does NotMatchedOnly drop partial lines? Can an item appear twice (prior-year line plus carry-forward line)? Can one entry have several partner lines? Folder-wide scope without CompanyIds is labelled an assumption. New items: a control check against SumDebit/SumCredit (H23), the documented fallback through account-histories.list, and a guard on the client path so that a ledger line whose book entry is already a kept open-sales row is never emitted again (no double count).
corrections.why: Horus guide › Outstanding items & matching: "Lines that are not matched yet make up the outstanding items" (F). suppliers.outstanding has "MatchStatus: number enum[0, 900] // - `0`: Partially - `900`: Totally", so partial lines are plausible but not confirmed. Open sales invoices carry "PaymentStatus ... `10`: Partially paid" natively, but suppliers have no such list. If partial lines are not returned, partially paid supplier invoices disappear without notice.

corrections.topic: Invoice vs credit-note classification on read
corrections.reference_said: Appendix B D1: "On read, always scan both daybook types and classify each entry as invoice or credit note from the sign of the customer/supplier line; for open sales items, the documented TransactionType takes precedence." Section 7 row "A credit note stored in a sales or purchase daybook" is labelled Assumption.
corrections.now: Proposed rule, daybook first: an entry in a 250/150 daybook is a credit note and an entry in a 200/100 daybook is an invoice. The partner-line sign is used only in folders without a credit-note daybook, where the write fallback posts refunds into 200/100, so the connector's own documents still round-trip. TransactionType on open sales items is a consistency check (mismatches are logged), never an override, so a document keeps its class once paid. Known failure, now stated: an accountant's credit note keyed into 200/100 in a folder that has 250/150 comes back as an invoice with negative amounts. Label A, pending H2 (Horus) and C5/C10 (Chift). Verdict text: "invoice/refund split conditional on H2".
corrections.why: Chift contract (InvoiceItemDueDatesOut.amount): "A negative amount represents credit on customer invoices and supplier refunds or debit on supplier invoices and customer refunds". Credit-direction invoices are therefore legitimate, and sign-first would file every one of them as a refund. TransactionType exists only on invoices.sales.outstanding.list (open items), so the reference override moved a document from customer_invoice to customer_refund once it was paid. Book entries expose no invoice type on read (H2).

corrections.topic: Documentation version and evidence base disclosure
corrections.reference_said: Section 2 Sources: "Horus API reference | 72 endpoint pages, each with its OpenAPI definition (documentation dated 24 September 2026)". The host is never named ("apiary" appears 0 times in the report), and nothing says that no live calls were made.
corrections.now: Sources state that the case links the former Horus documentation (horussoftwareapi.docs.apiary.io), while the analysis used the current documentation at docs.horus-software.be: API reference dated 24 Sep 2026, guides printed 13 Oct 2026, tax spreadsheets downloaded 13 Oct 2026. The two versions were not compared. New H20 (tier 1) asks which is authoritative and whether apiary is deprecated or covers another API version. Chift contract: the OpenAPI bundled in chift SDK 0.6.16; docs.chift.eu could not be reached and is to be spot-checked. Method: desk analysis, with no request sent to a Horus licence or a Chift environment.
corrections.why: case.md: "see documentation here: https://horussoftwareapi.docs.apiary.io/#introduction/general-principles". If names or fields differ between versions, the mapping would look wrong in the meeting. No allowed source shows whether they differ, so this is a disclosure, not a claim that the mapping is wrong.

corrections.reference_said: Invoice creation card: "invoice_number null: a draft gets Number=0. A posted sale gets max(DocumentNo)+1 from the same call (assumption, race risk) or is rejected. A posted purchase gets null (nullable)." C7: "Is rejecting non-numeric invoice and operation numbers acceptable?"
corrections.now: Proposal (C7, tier 1; H3): an entry pushed unconfirmed without a number carries Number 0, for sales and purchases alike (null is not used, because what Horus stores for it is undocumented). An invoice to be confirmed without invoice_number is pushed for review with Number 0 and returned as "draft" with invoice_number null (default). Alternatives: a 422, or max(DocumentNo)+1 as an opt-in after H3, with the race risk stated. Validation: non-numeric values, leading zeros, more than 15 digits and 0 are rejected with 422; the display number goes in reference. An entry without a number has no stable key after an accountant edit, so C7(c) asks whether the connector may require or assign one. operation_number is assumed to be the Horus entry Number (C7(d)).
corrections.why: invoices.sales.new: "Number *: number ... (can be 0 if not confirmed)"; invoices.purchases.new: "Number: number|null ... Nullable". AutoGenerateNumber exists only on misc, bank and financial operations ("Only works if \"Confirmed\" is set to *true*"). Chift: invoice_number "if not specified, will be automatically generated according to the system’s numbering rules. It does not necessarily match the number displayed on an invoice." Reconciling on daybook plus number fails for Number 0.

corrections.reference_said: Section 3 concept map: "VAT code | No VAT-code entity: rate + origin + type (+ kind and condition for purchases) | ... | Documented". Section 1: "Horus has no VAT-code entity". Task B: "Horus VatDetail.VatCode is Horus's internal code and is never returned as the Chift tax_code".
corrections.now: Horus has no VAT-code list endpoint and accepts no VAT code on write. On read, account-histories.list/.info, customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding return VatDetail.VatCode and VatHeading strings whose meaning is undocumented; nothing shows they are "internal". D2 stays the v1 design, and VatCode is never returned as tax_code. H1(e) asks whether VatCode is stable and one-to-one with a combination, TaxKind included. If it is, purchase tax_code = null on read could be removed.
corrections.why: appendix_horus_api_reference.md › account-histories.list: "VatCode: string|null // " and "VatHeading: string|null // ", with no description; the same fields appear on account-histories.info, customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding. Labelling an absence claim "Documented" when the reference shows a VAT code on read is an easy challenge.

corrections.topic: Chart-of-accounts type and type filters (VAT, cash)
corrections.reference_said: Chart-of-accounts card, items[].type (first match wins, label Derived): "(5) AccountSubCategory: '500: ADispo - \"Valeurs disponibles\"' → bank (bank vs cash is ambiguous)"; "(6) AccountCategory: ... '100: Assets', ... '600: Liability' and '1100: Prov' → other"; "(7) Fallback for Legislation BE only ...: 411 or 451 → vat, 55 → bank, 57 → cash". Overview: "POST /accounts.list, POST /daybooks.list (account type derivation, cached)".
corrections.now: Balance-sheet AccountCategory values now give "no conclusion", so the cascade reaches the BE prefix step. ADispo is resolved by prefix in BE folders (55 → bank, 57 → cash, otherwise bank). type=vat and type=cash are best effort. When a request asks for them, the connector loads the line-level AccountType map (account-histories.list over the current and previous fiscal year, one call per folder, cached), so accounts with movements are typed by "400: VAT" or "500: Cash". Unused accounts rely on the BE prefix fallback (A); in LU folders, unused VAT and cash accounts cannot be typed. The overview adds account-histories.list (only for a VAT or cash filter), and the impact reads "VAT and cash filters best effort". The row is labelled A. C18 asks how an inexact filter is reported; H12 adds the IntCategory list and "is AccountCategory always filled?".
corrections.why: Because the first match wins, step 6 typed every balance-sheet account, VAT accounts 411/451 included, as "other" before step 7 could run, and step 5 sent 57 accounts to bank. type=vat and type=cash therefore returned almost nothing. Chift's filter targets these uses (appendix_chift_spec_extract.md › GET chart-of-accounts: "Filter based on the type of the account (e.g. bank, cash, income, expense, vat)"). account-histories.list documents "AccountType ... 400: VAT - 500: Cash".

corrections.reference_said: Section 3 conventions: "Filters | String filters use “contains”; all filters must match. Many lists offer ModifiedAfter/ModifiedBefore for incremental synchronisation. Ledger periods are expressed in months. | Documented". Section 6 reference cache: "refreshed when a lookup misses".
corrections.now: In the API reference, ModifiedAfter/ModifiedBefore exist on three lists only: companies.list, book-entries.list and account-histories.list. Accounts, daybooks, cost schemas and sections, fiscal years, folders and the open-item lists have no change filter and are re-read in full; deletions are not signalled. As a result, the reference cache gets a short time-to-live on top of refresh-on-miss, and closure dates are read fresh before every write. For invoice retrieval with updated_after: ModifiedAfter, minus a small overlap (proposal), is applied to headers and lines; the look-back is bounded (C11); boundary semantics and whether line and matching changes are tracked go to H10; a periodic full reconciliation runs; consumers dedupe by id.
corrections.why: The guides say "Many lists also offer ModifiedAfter / ModifiedBefore filters" (Making requests) and name "companies.list , book-entries.list and account-histories.list among others" (Reading accounting data), but in appendix_horus_api_reference.md the filter appears only in those three request schemas. Refresh-on-miss cannot catch an account made inactive, a renamed daybook or a newly closed period.

corrections.topic: Client-visible limitations revised (new section 6), including the currency switch on read
corrections.reference_said: Section 1: "Data loss Chift should disclose to its clients: one address per third party, no mobile, notes or person fields; no line quantity or unit price on invoices; the account type cannot be written; miscellaneous operations are EUR-only; analytic balances are not stored." The read-side currency behaviour appears only in the invoice retrieval card: "only open foreign-currency sales invoices are returned in their own currency".
corrections.now: A new section 6, "Impact on client applications", in plain language, adds: invoice ids change when an entry is modified; a pushed invoice cannot be deleted through the integration; entries may wait for accountant review; purchase VAT codes can come back empty on read; every partner comes back as a company; numbers must be numeric. It also adds that a foreign-currency sales invoice comes back in its own currency while open and switches to euro once paid, and purchase invoices always come back in euro. C16 asks Chift to choose between this behaviour, disclosed, and one stable euro view until H4 (the analyst's preference). Reworded: misc operations are converted at the supplied rate (not "EUR-only"); analytic balances are not stored per account but can be computed over a period (C4), so they are not lost.
corrections.why: Invoice-currency amounts exist only on invoices.sales.outstanding.list ("TotalCurrencyAmount", "OpenCurrencyAmount"), which returns "open invoices (and/or linked payments) for a given folder". The currency of ledger amounts is undocumented (D4, H4). A syncing consumer would see the same id change currency and amounts once the invoice is paid. cost-histories.list makes period balances computable.

corrections.reference_said: Appendix B D7: "folder_id is required when a connection has several selected folders." Section 7 error translation: "403 Forbidden | The folder or resource is not accessible with this connection. | 400 “folder not accessible with this connection”".
corrections.now: Every folder-scoped route rejects a folder_id that is not in the stored activation selection with 400 "folder not selected for this connection", before any Horus call. This is defence in depth and is dropped if Chift confirms its platform enforces the rule upstream (C12). A Horus 403 maps to 400 "access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)". Get folders is not affected.
corrections.why: Chift FolderItem.selected: "Only selected folders can be used in subsequent requests. Requests targeting a folder that was not selected will be rejected." One Horus grant covers every folder the authorising user can see (folders.list Mode "`0`: All folders - For the accountant: All folders"), so on an accounting-firm licence isolation otherwise rests on Chift's selection alone. According to review S2-07, the reference enforced the check only in client creation.

corrections.topic: Write-route read-back counts and failed read-backs
corrections.reference_said: Section 1: "Creation calls return only an id. Client and account creation read the record back (one .info call) to return the full Chift response; invoices are read back by default, and miscellaneous operations only when Horus generates the number." Section 5 client intro: "reads the company back (company details, IBANs and the receivable account)". Invoice card: "If the read-back fails, never re-create the invoice: return the Id with echoed values."
corrections.now: Client creation needs two to three read-back calls: companies.info; ibans.list when the company has IBANs; accounts.info for the receivable account when the chart is not cached. A single companies.list call with Include is an assumption (H15). Account creation needs one accounts.info call. Invoices are read back by default; misc operations only when Horus generates the number. Values Horus cannot store (quantity, unit price, exact analytic percentages) are echoed, so a later read can differ. On every write route, a failed read-back never causes a re-create or an error; the response is built from the request values (D13).
corrections.why: data/create_client.json: companies.info "1 per Chift call"; ibans.list "0-1 per Chift call (skip when companies.info Data.Ibans is empty)"; accounts.info "0-1 per Chift call; usually replaced by the per-folder accounts.list cache". The reference stated the no-re-create rule only for invoices. Returning an error after a successful create invites a retry that creates a second entry, which cannot be deleted through the API.

corrections.reference_said: Section 1 tile: "40 of 72 Horus endpoints called, including optional ones". Section 4 invoice retrieval row: "GET /book-entries.info (single invoice)".
corrections.now: The tile now uses the same rule as appendix A: 35 of 72 endpoints, excluding connection-setup, unused optional and compensation endpoints. The reference still counts 72 endpoints (D15). The invoice retrieval row drops the single-invoice call, which the card places outside the route, and lists book-entries.info only for incremental reads where headers are missing for changed lines. The outstanding row adds account-histories.info, called once per open sales invoice missing from the customer ledger list (frequency depends on H8). Misc operations are no longer listed under the analytics percentage converter, since they carry one analytic account per line.
corrections.why: Review S1-16: the tile disagreed with appendix A (35 endpoints with a case-scope use) and with the route cards. The corrected build shows "35 of 72 Horus endpoints called, including optional ones".

questions.short: Are the Horus tax-combination spreadsheets current, complete and authoritative for Belgian and Luxembourg folders (they differ from the API reference in places), and how are changes announced? How is an invalid combination rejected, and what do the VAT codes returned on read represent?
questions.why: Every invoice’s VAT translation and the VAT-code list depend on this catalogue.

questions.short: Can credit notes and invoices be posted in each other’s daybooks, and can the document type be exposed on read? Which signs apply to credit notes, and are negative lines or negative invoice totals accepted?
questions.why: Decides daybook choice and sign rules on write, and invoice versus refund classification on read.

questions.short: How are duplicate document numbers detected and rejected? Is there an idempotency key or a safe way to retry after a timeout? How are invoices and operations numbered when sent without a number?
questions.why: Duplicate protection, safe retries after timeouts, and numbering of entries sent without a number.

questions.short: For foreign-currency documents, which currency are amounts in on create and on read, can original-currency amounts be recovered for paid and purchase invoices, which way is the rate quoted, and is the folder currency always EUR?
questions.why: Correct amounts on write and on read for every foreign-currency document.

questions.short: Are there rate limits, timeouts, or caps on result size or date range for list endpoints, given they have no paging? Could account histories be fetched for several companies in one call?
questions.why: Lists cannot be paged and some routes need one call per daybook; behaviour on large folders is unverified.

questions.short: Which error types can the API return (duplicates, closed period, invalid tax combination, unknown account), which status does an id from another folder return, and do create endpoints themselves refuse dates in closed periods?
questions.why: Precise errors for Chift consumers, safe retry rules, and whether the connector’s closed-period check is the only guard.

questions.short: What are the rules for company and account search keys, are cost-section keys and external references unique per folder, and does Horus generate a company search key when none is sent?
questions.why: The connector generates company search keys, validates account numbers and finds partners by external reference.

questions.short: Do the outstanding-item endpoints return every open item of all partners, uncapped and without duplicates, including partially matched and carried-forward items? Are amounts original or remaining, can one invoice carry several due dates, and is a purchase-side open-invoice list planned?
questions.why: Decides whether outstanding items are complete, how supplier open amounts are computed, and the call pattern.

questions.short: Where does the invoice header comment appear when the invoice is read back?
questions.why: Round-trip of reference and customer memo.

questions.short: Do date filters use calendar months or accounting periods, and do an API invoice’s period and VAT month always follow its date? Does the modified-after filter catch line and matching changes? Do accountant edits change entry ids or numbers, and are deletions signalled?
questions.why: Reliable incremental synchronisation and date filtering.

questions.short: What do several company fields mean (suspended activity, second name and address, family, contact person), how is an enterprise number written, which collective account applies by default, and does invoice creation check the partner’s customer or supplier flag?
questions.why: Mapping of active status, addresses, company numbers and receivable accounts, and partner checks on invoice creation.

questions.short: Can an account’s category be set, or is it derived from the number? What is the full list of categories, is it always filled for balance-sheet accounts, and does the account list include inactive and title accounts?
questions.why: Determines the Chift account type on creation and in the chart of accounts.

questions.short: How do analytics behave: what is returned for folders without the analytics module, which cost schemas must each line carry (rounding lines included), are there limits on cost lines, what do the schema flags mean, and is the cost-history balance signed?
questions.why: Analytics on write and the analytic routes on read.

questions.short: What does the daybook “used” flag mean, which daybook types accept API entries, does the fiscal-year list show whether a year is closed, and is a miscellaneous operation dated in a closed operations or VAT period refused, with which error?
questions.why: Journal flags and posting rules.

questions.short: Which related data can be included in the same call on the company, book-entry and account-history lists, and with which fields?
questions.why: Could reduce read-backs and invoice retrieval to fewer calls.

questions.short: Can fetching a single entry by id return an entry from another folder of the same license? What does it return for a replaced or deleted entry, and does a replaced entry link to its successor?
questions.why: Read-backs and single-invoice reads.

questions.short: Can Chift get a test license or test folder, can test data be removed (the API cannot delete companies or invoices), and are test licenses hosted like production?
questions.why: The API works on live data, and the volume test must reflect production conditions.

questions.short: What is the maximum attachment size for uploads?
questions.why: Validation of PDFs sent with invoices.

questions.short: How does Chift register an integration (client credentials, redirect URIs, approval), and which Horus user should authorise the connection for an accounting firm and for an SMB so the right folders are visible?
questions.why: Registration is the first step, and the folders visible through the API depend on the authorising user’s access.

questions.short: Is docs.horus-software.be the authoritative API documentation, and is the apiary version linked in the case deprecated or for a different API version?
questions.why: Every mapping rests on the current documentation; the two versions were not compared.

questions.short: May every integration and user type confirm entries through the API, or can the accounting firm restrict it? What is blocked once confirmed, is confirmation the accountant’s final validation, and do unconfirmed entries count in balances, VAT returns and closings?
questions.why: Decides whether direct posting can be offered on every connection and what “draft” means for clients.

questions.short: How does Horus validate invoice amounts: does it refuse or recalculate VAT more than one cent off base × rate, how are header and line totals compared, is a zero-base line with VAT accepted, and which decimal precision applies?
questions.why: Defines how the connector books VAT and rounding.

questions.short: For outstanding items: which account types can be returned, do the summary totals cover exactly the returned lines, are unlinked or partly allocated payments returned, and does the confirmed-only filter also keep unconfirmed elements out of open amounts?
questions.why: Control totals, signs and completeness of the outstanding items route.

questions.short: How do OAuth connections behave over their lifecycle: valid license API host patterns, repeated authorisations by the same user, tokens after the user loses access, lost refresh responses, revocation by the integrator, and refresh-token lifetimes?
questions.why: Safe activation, token-store design and offboarding for Chift’s multi-tenant connections.

questions.short: On client creation: are contact fields returned on read, how are VAT and enterprise numbers stored, normalised and checked for duplicates (per folder or license, also on update), and does one invalid IBAN fail the whole create?
questions.why: Round-trip of the client response, duplicate checks and error handling on client creation.

questions.short: Should each connection choose a posting mode, review (entries pushed unconfirmed for the accountant; proposed default) or direct (confirmed on push), possibly per folder? Is returning the status actually stored acceptable, and what does “draft” mean across Chift connectors?
questions.why: Confirmation in Horus means accountant validation, changes numbering and limits deletion; the API cannot delete invoices.

questions.short: Is a connector-built VAT-code list per folder (from the Horus tax-combination files) acceptable, with tax_code null on read when ambiguous? Should OSS codes cover only requested countries, and should consumer VAT amounts be booked exactly as sent (proposed)?
questions.why: Horus has no VAT-code list, accepts no VAT code on write, and its read-side VAT code is undocumented.

questions.short: For inputs Horus cannot store (for example withholding tax, accrual dates, line quantity, extra addresses, more than two decimals), should the connector reject or drop them? Which address wins when several are sent, and is connector-side logging enough without a warnings field?
questions.why: Consistent behaviour across Chift connectors.

questions.short: For values Horus does not hold, should reads return null or a default? Is the folder country worth one extra call per folder? Should create responses echo unstored request fields or match what a later read returns?
questions.why: Avoids misleading defaults and create responses that differ from later reads.

questions.short: Sign conventions: are refunds sent positive, discounts as negative lines, and negative invoice totals allowed? Without a readable document type, which misclassification is preferable? Should credit notes and unallocated payments be negative in outstanding items, and partial payments allocated oldest due date first?
questions.why: Input sign is unspecified, Horus hides document type on read, and invoice and outstanding views would sign credit notes differently.

questions.short: On a duplicate (VAT number, external reference, document number, or supplier, date and total for unnumbered bills), return an error or the existing record? Which error for a timed-out create with unknown outcome? How should force_merge combine client and supplier data?
questions.why: Duplicate and merge policy must match other connectors; Horus has no idempotency key and one identity per company.

questions.short: Is rejecting non-numeric numbers acceptable? For an invoice to be confirmed without a number: push as draft for review (proposed), reject, or generate the next number? May numbers be required, and is operation_number the entry number or a client reference?
questions.why: Horus does not number invoices itself and stores numbers as numbers; unnumbered entries cannot be found after accountant edits.

questions.short: What does partner_info.account_number mean, and is partner_info needed when Horus can create partners? Should a missing customer or supplier role be added or rejected, how should new third-party codes be generated, and how should same-name clients without identifiers be handled?
questions.why: account_number is undefined in the Chift spec, the code is visible to accountants, and unidentified clients cannot be reliably deduplicated.

questions.short: Is building analytic combinations from independent per-plan percentages acceptable? Should Free-type Horus dimensions be hidden from analytic plans (proposed)? Are slightly different read-back distributions on small amounts acceptable, and should plans covering only part of a line be omitted?
questions.why: Horus allocates amounts to combinations of cost sections.

questions.short: Should unconfirmed entries be returned as drafts or excluded by default? Is an invoice id changing after an accountant edit acceptable? Do consumers rely on updated_after for status changes like “paid”, and what periodic full re-sync is acceptable?
questions.why: In review mode every pushed invoice stays unconfirmed until the accountant confirms it; excluding them by default would hide them.

questions.short: What default period should invoice retrieval use without dates (proposed: current fiscal year), how far back must updated_after polls look, and are consumers expected to dedupe items re-sent by a safety overlap?
questions.why: Horus needs a month window and cannot page lists; the default and look-back drive the cost of every read.

questions.short: Should the Horus connector always enable multiple folders? Does the platform block folder ids not selected at activation, or must the connector? Can several Chift consumers share one Horus license, and who activates the connector for a firm-managed SMB?
questions.why: Accounting-firm licenses hold many folders, and one Horus token sees every folder its user can access.

questions.short: Documentation remark, no decision needed: main_currency cites ISO 3166-1 (a country standard) instead of ISO 4217, and the line tax_amount formula omits the division by 100.
questions.why: Small corrections to the Chift API reference.

questions.short: Can a connector cache reference data per folder, and results between page calls of one request? What is the synchronous request timeout, and is there a background pattern for heavy reads?
questions.why: Horus lists cannot be paged; without a cache every page call re-reads the whole period.

questions.short: For foreign-currency miscellaneous operations, does Chift core convert amounts to EUR before calling the connector, or must the connector? Which rate direction applies, how is a rounding residue absorbed, and should the response show the original currency or EUR?
questions.why: Horus operation lines have no currency field, and Chift requires a rate for operations in another currency.

questions.short: Horus gives original-currency amounts on read only for open sales invoices. Keep that (invoices switch to euro once paid), or always return foreign-currency invoices in EUR at rate 1 (favoured)? Which rate direction, and are mixed-currency outstanding items acceptable?
questions.why: Consumers syncing with updated_after would see an invoice change currency; Chift does not define the rate direction.

questions.short: For outstanding items: one item per invoice with several due dates, or one per due-date line (proposed)? Should unallocated payments and credit balances appear? Are per-partner matching numbers acceptable as they are, and should employee items be excluded?
questions.why: Chift lists all due dates per item while Horus has one per ledger line; this changes open items and totals.

questions.short: When a list filter cannot be applied exactly on Horus (approval status, unknown journal id, estimated account types), return 400, ignore it, or return a best-effort result? Is Horus “Verified” an acceptable stand-in for “approved”?
questions.why: Silent empty or approximate results are hard for consumers to detect; behaviour should match other connectors.

questions.short: On invoice creation, how large a header/line difference may invoice_correction absorb before rejection, and should lines whose tax departs from untaxed amount × rate beyond a tolerance be rejected?
questions.why: Without limits, real data errors would be booked on the correction account or as VAT.

questions.short: Which status and error_code do other connectors use for validation errors without a predefined code, re-authorisation, persistent upstream errors and unknown create outcomes? Should VAT numbers with dots or spaces be rejected or normalised, and does the platform retry after timeouts?
questions.why: Consumers branch on status and error_code, which must match other connectors.
